title.zh: 卷二十一 志第十一 禮下
title.raw: 卷二十一 志第十一 禮下 Volume 21 Treatises 11: Rites Part Three

sentences.zh: 禮志下

translations.literal: Section heading: Treatise on Rites, lower fascicle.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise on Rites, Part Three

sentences.zh: 五禮之別，三曰賓，蓋朝宗、覲遇、會同之制是也。

translations.literal: Among the categories of the five rites, the third is called "guest"; these are the regulations for paying homage at court (朝宗), audiences (覲遇), and joint gatherings (會同).
translations.idiomatic: The third of the five ritual categories is "guest," covering homage at court, formal audiences, and great assemblies where states meet together.

sentences.zh: 自周以下，其禮彌繁。

translations.literal: From the Zhou onward, its rituals grew ever more elaborate.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhou period, ritual grew steadily more complex.

sentences.zh: 自秦滅學之後，舊典殘缺。

translations.literal: After the Qin destroyed learning, old statutes survived only in fragments.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Qin campaign against scholarship had passed, the classical ritual corpus lay broken and incomplete.

sentences.zh: 漢興，始使叔孫通制禮，參用先代之儀，然亦往往改異焉。

translations.literal: When the Han arose, they first ordered Shu Sun Tong to compile ritual, mixing in ceremonies from earlier dynasties, yet they also frequently altered them.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Han, Shu Sun Tong was commissioned to frame court ritual, borrowing forms from antiquity while revising them repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 漢儀有正會禮，正旦，夜漏未盡七刻，鐘鳴受賀，公侯以下執贄夾庭，二千石以上升殿稱萬歲，然後作樂宴饗。

translations.literal: The Han regulations included the grand New Year's assembly rite: on New Year's Day, before the clepsydra had seven marks left in the night watch, the bell sounded and they received congratulations; marquises and below brought tribute gifts lined along the courtyard; those ranked two thousand shi and above ascended the hall and shouted "long life"; then music was performed and a banquet held.
translations.idiomatic: Han ceremony prescribed the formal New Year's audience: while night still had seven marks to run, bells rang to open the congratulations; nobles presented gifts along the court; officials at two thousand shi and above mounted the hall to hail the throne before music and feasting began.

sentences.zh: 魏武帝都鄴，正會文昌殿，用漢儀，又設百華燈。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Wei made his capital at Ye and held the New Year's assembly in Wenchang Hall, following Han ritual and also setting out the "hundred-flower" lanterns.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao ruled Wei from Ye, the New Year's audience took place in Wenchang Hall under Han precedents, illuminated by elaborate tiered lanterns.

sentences.zh: 晉氏受命，武帝更定元會儀，《咸寧注》是也。

translations.literal: When the Jin received the mandate, Emperor Wu revised the New Year's court ritual; this is what the Xianning commentary records.
translations.idiomatic: Under the new Jin dynasty, Emperor Wu promulgated a revised protocol for the New Year's audience, codified in the Xianning commentary.

sentences.zh: 傅玄《元會賦》曰：「考夏後之遺訓，綜殷周之典藝，采秦漢之舊儀，定元正之嘉會。

translations.literal: Fu Xuan's "Rhapsody on the New Year's Assembly" says: "He examined the teachings handed down from the Xia house, drew together the models of Yin and Zhou, took up the old observances of Qin and Han, and fixed the splendid gathering that opens the year."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan wrote in his "Rhapsody on the New Year's Assembly": "Tracing the Xia legacy, weaving Yin–Zhou precedent with Qin–Han court forms, he instituted the splendid ceremony that marks the first day of the year."

sentences.zh: 」此則兼采眾代可知矣。

translations.literal: From this one knows it drew on many successive ages.
translations.idiomatic: The liturgy thus consciously synthesized ritual from successive dynasties.

sentences.zh: 《咸寧注》：「先正一日，有司各宿設。

translations.literal: The Xianning commentary states: "On the day before, each office lodges overnight to prepare.
translations.idiomatic: Per the Xianning commentary, officials bivouac in the palace the eve before to prepare.

sentences.zh: 夜漏未盡十刻，群臣集到，庭燎起火。

translations.literal: Before the clepsydra had ten marks left in the night watch, the assembled ministers arrived; torches were lit in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: While ten night marks still remained, ministers gathered as courtyard beacon-fires were kindled.

sentences.zh: 上賀，起，謁報，又賀皇后。

translations.literal: They congratulated the Sovereign; he rose; they reported and withdrew; then they congratulated the empress.
translations.idiomatic: They offered New Year's felicitations to the emperor, who rose while petitions were announced, then felicitations were extended to the empress.

sentences.zh: 還，從雲龍東中華門入，詣東閣下，便坐。

translations.literal: Returning, they entered through the middle gate of Yunlong on the east and proceeded to below the eastern arcade, where informal seats were taken.
translations.idiomatic: They returned indoors through the eastern portal of the Yunlong Gate and waited informally beneath the eastern cloister.

sentences.zh: 漏未盡七刻，百官及受贄郎官以下至計吏皆入立其次，其陛衛者如臨軒儀。

translations.literal: Before the clepsydra had seven marks left, all officials, together with tribute-bearing gentlemen and clerks down to the accounting officers, entered and stood in their stations; those guarding the stairways followed the protocol used when the emperor faced south from the hall.
translations.idiomatic: With seven marks left before dawn, every rank from tribute presenters down to county clerks took assigned places while stair guards mirrored the formation for a formal imperial appearance.

sentences.zh: 漏未盡五刻，謁者、僕射、大鴻臚各各奏群臣就位定。

translations.literal: Before five marks remained, the usher directors, masters of attendance, and senior herald each reported that the ministers were in position.
translations.idiomatic: At five marks the usher superintendents, masters of attendance, and chief herald successively announced that the assembly was set.

sentences.zh: 漏盡，侍中奏外辦。

translations.literal: When the water ran out, the palace attendant reported that preparations outside were complete.
translations.idiomatic: At the moment the night measure emptied, an attendant declared the outer court ready.

sentences.zh: 皇帝出，鐘鼓作，百官皆拜伏。

translations.literal: The emperor emerged; bells and drums sounded; all officials bowed prone.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appeared to bells and drums as the throng dropped to full prostration.

sentences.zh: 太常導皇帝升御坐，鐘鼓止，百官起。

translations.literal: The Chamberlain for Ceremonial guided the emperor to the imperial seat; bells and drums ceased and the officials rose.
translations.idiomatic: The Chamberlain for Ceremonial escorted him to the throne; music stopped and the assembly stood.

sentences.zh: 大鴻臚跪奏'請朝賀'。

translations.literal: The senior herald knelt and announced: "We ask that congratulations be received."
translations.idiomatic: The chief herald knelt to pray leave for the congratulatory presentation.

sentences.zh: 掌禮郎贊'皇帝延王登'。

translations.literal: The ritual usher intoned: "The emperor invites the kings to ascend."
translations.idiomatic: Masters of ritual called for the imperial clansmen to approach the dais.

sentences.zh: 大鴻臚跪贊'籓王臣某等奉白璧各一，再拜賀'。

translations.literal: The senior herald knelt and proclaimed: "The vassal kings, Your Majesty's servants So-and-so, present white jade discs, each one, and bow twice in congratulations."
translations.idiomatic: The herald knelt to announce each enfeoffed prince presenting a white jade tally with double bows of homage.

sentences.zh: 太常報'王悉登'。

translations.literal: The Chamberlain for Ceremonial answered: "Let all kings ascend."
translations.idiomatic: The Chamberlain for Ceremonial replied that every prince might mount the steps.

sentences.zh: 謁者引上殿，當御坐。

translations.literal: Ushers led them onto the hall opposite the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: Guided by ushers, they advanced to stations facing the throne.

sentences.zh: 皇帝興，王再拜。

translations.literal: The emperor rose; the kings bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign stood while the princes performed the double obeisance.

sentences.zh: 皇帝坐，復再拜。

translations.literal: The emperor sat; they bowed twice again.
translations.idiomatic: Once he was seated they repeated the double bow.

sentences.zh: 跪置璧御坐前，復再拜。

translations.literal: They knelt and placed the jade before the imperial seat, then bowed twice again.
translations.idiomatic: Kneeling, they laid their discs before the throne and bowed twice more.

sentences.zh: 成禮訖，謁者引下殿，還故位。

translations.literal: When the ceremony finished, ushers led them down from the hall back to their original positions.
translations.idiomatic: At its conclusion escorts conducted them off the dais to their former ranks.

sentences.zh: 掌禮郎贊'皇帝延太尉等'。

translations.literal: The ritual usher intoned: "The emperor invites the grand commandant and the others to ascend."
translations.idiomatic: The ritual usher next summoned the Grand Commandant and fellow dignitaries.

sentences.zh: 於是公、特進、匈奴南單于、金紫將軍當大鴻臚西，中二千石、二千石、千石、六百石當大行令西，皆北面伏。

translations.literal: Thereupon dukes, specially promoted seniors, the Southern Xiongnu chanyu, and gold-purple generals stood west of the chief herald; ministerial officials at rank-two thousand, two thousand, one thousand, and six hundred shi lined west of the Director of Grand Processions—all faced north in prone posture.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes, extraordinary appointees, the Southern Shanyu, and gold-purple generals arrayed west of the herald; ministers from two thousand shi down to six hundred shi faced north west of the Grand Processions director.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚跪贊'太尉、中二千石等奉璧、皮、帛、羔、雁、雉，再拜賀'。

translations.literal: The herald knelt and announced: "The grand commandant and those at two thousand shi present jade, hides, silk, lamb, wild goose, and pheasant, and bow twice in congratulations."
translations.idiomatic: The herald listed offerings—discs, pelts, silk, lamb, goose, and pheasant—from the Grand Commandant's party with double bows.

sentences.zh: 太常贊'皇帝延公等登'。

translations.literal: The Chamberlain for Ceremonial called: "The emperor invites the dukes and others to ascend."
translations.idiomatic: The Chamberlain for Ceremonial bade the dukes and colleagues mount the hall.

sentences.zh: 掌禮引公至金紫將軍上殿。

translations.literal: Ritual ushers guided the dukes up until they stood above the gold-purple generals.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants shepherded the dukes past the gold-purple generals toward the throne.

sentences.zh: 皇帝興，皆再拜。

translations.literal: The emperor rose; all bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rose again as everyone doubled their bows.

sentences.zh: 皇帝坐，又再拜。

translations.literal: The emperor sat; again they bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: When he resumed his seat they repeated the obeisance.

sentences.zh: 跪置璧皮帛御坐前，復再拜。

translations.literal: They knelt and laid jade, hides, and silk before the imperial seat, then bowed twice again.
translations.idiomatic: Kneeling, they deposited discs, pelts, and fabrics before the throne and bowed twice more.

sentences.zh: 成禮訖，謁者引下殿，還故位。

translations.literal: When the rite ended, ushers led them down and returned them to their stations.
translations.idiomatic: Finished, they were conducted down as before.

sentences.zh: 公置璧成禮時，大行令並贊殿下，中二千石以下同。

translations.literal: While the dukes were placing their jade and completing the ceremony, the Director of Grand Processions simultaneously intoned from below the steps; those beneath chief ministers at two thousand shi followed the same cadence.
translations.idiomatic: As dukes completed their presentations, the Grand Processions director coordinated responses from below the stairs for everyone under chief minister rank.

sentences.zh: 成禮訖，以贄授贄郎，郎以璧帛付謁者，羔、雁、雉付太官。

translations.literal: When the ceremony concluded, the tribute was handed to tribute gentlemen; they passed discs and silk to ushers and delivered lamb, goose, and pheasant to the imperial kitchens.
translations.idiomatic: Offerings went from presenters to tribute clerks, then discs and cloth to ushers while meats went to the palace stewards.

sentences.zh: 太樂令跪請奏雅樂，樂以次作。

translations.literal: The Director of Music knelt and asked permission to perform the classical suites; music proceeded in proper sequence.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Music sought leave to strike the canonical hymns in prescribed order.

sentences.zh: 乘黃令乃出車，皇帝罷入，百官皆坐。

translations.literal: The Director of the Yellow Carriages then brought out the chariots; the emperor withdrew and the officials all sat.
translations.idiomatic: The chariot master rolled out state vehicles; the emperor retired and ministers took seats.

sentences.zh: 晝漏上水六刻，諸蠻夷胡客以次入，皆再拜訖，坐。

translations.literal: Six marks after the day measure began, foreign envoys and tribal guests entered in turn; each finished the double bow and sat.
translations.idiomatic: Six marks into daylight, barbarian envoys entered by roster, bowed twice, and seated themselves.

sentences.zh: 禦入後三刻又出，鐘鼓作。

translations.literal: Three marks after the imperial palanquin had entered, he emerged again to bells and drums.
translations.idiomatic: Three marks after the imperial litter withdrew indoors, he reappeared with bells and drums.

sentences.zh: 謁者、僕射跪奏'請群臣上'。

translations.literal: The usher directors and masters of attendance knelt and announced: "We ask that the ministers ascend."
translations.idiomatic: Ushers knelt to request that civil officials approach.

sentences.zh: 謁者引王公二千石上殿，千石、六百石停本位。

translations.literal: Ushers led royal dukes and those at two thousand shi onto the hall; those at one thousand and six hundred shi remained in place.
translations.idiomatic: Only nobles and two-thousand-shi officers mounted the steps while lower ranks stayed below.

sentences.zh: 謁者引王詣樽酌壽酒，跪授侍中，侍中跪置御坐前。

translations.literal: An usher guided a royal prince to the goblet of longevity wine, knelt, and handed it to the palace attendant, who knelt and set it before the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: A prince was led to the longevity cup, knelt, and passed it to an attendant who placed it before the throne.

sentences.zh: 王還。

translations.literal: The prince returned.
translations.idiomatic: The prince withdrew to his station.

sentences.zh: 王自酌置位前。

translations.literal: The prince poured for himself and set the cup before his own position.
translations.idiomatic: He filled his own cup and set it before his mat.

sentences.zh: 謁者跪奏'籓王臣某等奉觴，再拜上千萬歲壽'。

translations.literal: The usher knelt and announced: "The vassal kings, Your Majesty's servants So-and-so, raise this cup and bow twice, wishing Your Majesty ten thousand years of life."
translations.idiomatic: The herald announced the princes' toast with double bows wishing boundless longevity.

sentences.zh: 四廂樂作，百官再拜。

translations.literal: Music from the four sides began; all officials bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: Ensemble music struck up from every corner as the assembly bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 已飲，又再拜。

translations.literal: After drinking, they bowed twice again.
translations.idiomatic: They drank, then bowed twice once more.

sentences.zh: 謁者引王等還本位。

translations.literal: Ushers led the kings back to their places.
translations.idiomatic: Escorts returned the princes to their ranks.

sentences.zh: 陛下者傳就席，群臣皆跪諾。

translations.literal: Those who conveyed court etiquette passed word for all to take seats; the assembled ministers knelt and assented.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial heralds signaled everyone to sit; ministers knelt their acknowledgment.

sentences.zh: 侍中、中書令、尚書令各于殿上上壽酒。

translations.literal: Palace attendants, secretariat directors, and secretariat chiefs each offered longevity wine from their positions on the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants, Palace Secretariat directors, and chiefs of the Secretariat presented longevity cups from the hall floor.

sentences.zh: 登歌樂升，太官又行禦酒。

translations.literal: The ascending-hymn musicians rose while the imperial kitchens again circulated imperial wine.
translations.idiomatic: Hymn singers began as palace stewards poured another round of imperial wine.

sentences.zh: 禦酒升階，太官令跪授侍郎，侍郎跪進御坐前。

translations.literal: As imperial wine ascended the stairs, the Chief Steward for the Imperial Kitchen knelt and handed it to the gentleman attendant, who knelt and advanced it before the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: Kitchen stewards passed cups up the stairs to gentleman attendants who knelt them before the throne.

sentences.zh: 乃行百官酒。

translations.literal: Then wine was offered to the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: The same courtesy extended down the ranks.

sentences.zh: 太樂令跪奏'奏登歌'，三終乃降。

translations.literal: The Director of Music knelt and announced: "We perform the ascending hymn," and after three stanzas they ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Music requested the ascending hymn, performed through three movements before stopping.

sentences.zh: 太官令跪請具禦飯，到階，群臣皆起。

translations.literal: The Chief Steward knelt and asked that the imperial meal be served; when it reached the steps, all officials rose.
translations.idiomatic: When stewards announced the imperial repast and trays reached the stairs, everyone stood.

sentences.zh: 太官令持羹跪授司徒，持飯跪授大司農，尚食持案並授持節，持節跪進御坐前。

translations.literal: The Chief Steward held the stew kneeling and handed it to the minister of education; he held the rice kneeling and handed it to the minister of agriculture; imperial servers carried trays together to the credential bearers, who knelt and advanced them before the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: Stewards relayed broth to the Minister of Education and grain to the Minister of Agriculture while synchronized servers knelt dishes before the throne.

sentences.zh: 群臣就席。

translations.literal: The assembled ministers took their mats.
translations.idiomatic: Officials settled at their banquet places.

sentences.zh: 太樂令跪奏'奏食舉樂'。

translations.literal: The Director of Music knelt and announced: "We perform the banquet music."
translations.idiomatic: Music masters requested the banquet suite.

sentences.zh: 太官行百官飯案遍。

translations.literal: The imperial kitchens circulated meal trays to every official.
translations.idiomatic: Palace kitchens served every rank in turn.

sentences.zh: 食畢，太樂令跪奏'請進樂'。

translations.literal: When the meal ended, the Director of Music knelt and asked to proceed with further music.
translations.idiomatic: After dining, musicians sought permission for the next entertainment.

sentences.zh: 樂以次作。

translations.literal: Music followed in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Performances continued in appointed order.

sentences.zh: 鼓吹令又前跪奏'請以次進眾妓'。

translations.literal: The director of wind and percussion again knelt and announced: "We ask that the entertainers enter in turn."
translations.idiomatic: The herald of drum-and-pipe bands asked leave to bring on troupes in rotation.

sentences.zh: 乃召諸郡計吏前，受敕戒於階下。

translations.literal: They then summoned the accounting officers of the commanderies forward to receive admonitions and instructions below the steps.
translations.idiomatic: County accountants were called forward for imperial injunctions at the foot of the stairs.

sentences.zh: 宴樂畢，謁者一人跪奏'請罷退'。

translations.literal: When the banquet ended, a single usher knelt and announced: "We ask permission to dismiss."
translations.idiomatic: As festivities closed, one usher knelt to seek leave to retire the court.

sentences.zh: 鐘鼓作，群臣北面再拜，出。

translations.literal: Bells and drums sounded; all ministers bowed twice toward the north and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Bells and drums marked their exit as the throng bowed north and departed.

sentences.zh: 」然則，夜漏未盡七刻謂之晨賀。

translations.literal: Thus what is called the "dawn congratulations" is when the night clepsydra still has seven marks left.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the "morning congratulations" were fixed while seven night marks yet remained.

sentences.zh: 晝漏上三刻更出，百官奉壽酒，謂之晝會。

translations.literal: Three marks after the day measure began he appeared again; officials presented longevity wine—this is called the daytime session.
translations.idiomatic: His second appearance three marks into daylight, when ministers offered longevity wine, was the midday audience.

sentences.zh: 別置女樂三十人于黃帳外，奏房中之歌。

translations.literal: Thirty female musicians were stationed outside the yellow canopy to perform chamber songs.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty female musicians beyond the yellow awning sang inner-chamber airs.

sentences.zh: 江左多虞，不復晨賀。

translations.literal: South of the Yangzi there were many alarms, so they no longer held the dawn congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: The refugee court faced constant crisis and abandoned the predawn felicitation.

sentences.zh: 夜漏未盡十刻，開宣陽門，至平旦始開殿門，晝漏上五刻，皇帝乃出受賀。

translations.literal: Before ten marks were left in the night watch they opened Xuanyang Gate; hall doors opened only at daybreak; five marks after the day clepsydra began the emperor emerged to receive congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: They opened Xuanyang Gate while ten night marks remained, kept palace gates shut until dawn, and brought the emperor out five marks into daylight for felicitations.

sentences.zh: 皇太子出會者，則在三恪下王公上。

translations.literal: When the heir apparent attended, he ranked below the three honored guests but above royal dukes.
translations.idiomatic: If the crown prince attended, he stood beneath the three hosts of honor but above enfeoffed princes.

sentences.zh: 正旦元會，設白獸樽於殿庭，樽蓋上施白獸，若有能獻直言者，則發此樽飲酒。

translations.literal: At the New Year's grand assembly they set a white-beast goblet in the courtyard; its lid bore a white beast, and whoever wished to speak bluntly could open this goblet and drink.
translations.idiomatic: New Year's court placed a "white beast" wine vessel in the courtyard—lifting its beast-shaped lid allowed a speaker of blunt counsel to drink.

sentences.zh: 案禮，白獸樽乃杜舉之遺式也，為白獸蓋，是後代所為，示忌憚也。

translations.literal: According to ritual precedent the white-beast goblet preserves the model of Du Ju's warning cup; adding a white beast to the lid was a later innovation meant to show awe and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Canon identifies the vessel with Du Ju's frank-speaking cup; the beast-embellished lid was a later symbolic warning.

sentences.zh: 魏制，籓王不得朝覲。

translations.literal: Under Wei regulations enfeoffed kings were not permitted court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Wei law barred imperial princes from routine audiences.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝時，有朝者皆由特恩，不得以為常。

translations.literal: In Emperor Ming's reign those who appeared did so only by special grace and could not treat it as ordinary practice.
translations.idiomatic: Under Ming only extraordinary favors brought princes to court—never as a standing rule.

sentences.zh: 及泰始中，有司奏：「諸侯之國，其王公以下入朝者，四方各為二番，三歲而周，周則更始。

translations.literal: And in the Taishi era the relevant offices memorialized: "In the domains of the feudal lords, whenever kings and dukes below come to court, each quarter of the realm supplies two rotations that cycle once every three years, then begin anew.
translations.idiomatic: During Taishi officials submitted: "Feudatories should rotate two cohorts per quadrant, each prince attending once every three years before the cycle renews."

sentences.zh: 若臨時有故，卻在明年。

translations.literal: If temporary circumstances arise, defer to the following year.
translations.idiomatic: Sudden obstacles postpone attendance until the next year.

sentences.zh: 明年來朝之後，更滿三歲乃復朝，不得違本數。

translations.literal: After coming to court the next year, three full years must pass again before another audience—do not violate the basic reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Once a prince has attended, another three-year interval must elapse before he returns—honor the statutory spacing.

sentences.zh: 朝禮皆親執璧，如舊朝之制。

translations.literal: Court ritual requires each to bear his own jade disc personally, following the old audience regulations.
translations.idiomatic: They must personally carry ritual jade as under earlier audience law.

sentences.zh: 不朝之歲，各遣卿奉聘。

translations.literal: In years without court visits each domain dispatches a minister on diplomatic duty.
translations.idiomatic: Off years send chief ministers bearing diplomatic missions.

sentences.zh: 」奏可。

translations.literal: " The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne endorsed the proposal.

sentences.zh: 江左王侯不之國，其有受任居外，則同方伯刺史二千石之禮，亦無朝聘之制，故此禮遂廢。

translations.literal: South of the Yangzi the noble houses never went out to their fiefs; when someone held office abroad he followed the etiquette of a regional inspector or two-thousand-shi governor, and there was likewise no system of court visits or diplomatic missions, so these observances lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Jin princes seldom took up their domains; those serving as provincial governors observed regional commissioner etiquette instead, and formal homage rotations vanished.

sentences.zh: 漢以高帝十月定秦，且為歲首。

translations.literal: The Han, because Gaozu subdued Qin in the tenth month, took that month as the year's beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Han reckoning treated the tenth month—when Gaozu pacified Qin—as New Year's start.

sentences.zh: 至武帝，雖改用夏正，然每月朔朝，至於十月朔，猶常饗會。

translations.literal: Down to Emperor Wu, although they switched to the Xia calendar, still each month they held dawn court on new moon day; as for the tenth month's new moon, they habitually continued the feast assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Though Emperor Wu adopted the Xia calendar, monthly new-moon audiences persisted, and the tenth-month gathering remained a banquet fixture.

sentences.zh: 其儀，夜漏未盡七刻，受賀及贄。

translations.literal: The protocol: before seven marks remained in the night watch they received congratulations and tribute gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Custom dictated felicitations and gift presentations while seven night marks still flowed.

sentences.zh: 公侯璧，中二千石、二千石羔，千石、六百石雁，四百石以下雉。

translations.literal: Marquises presented jade discs; chief ministers at two thousand shi presented lamb; those at one thousand and six hundred shi presented wild geese; four hundred shi and below presented pheasants.
translations.idiomatic: Rank determined tribute: discs for marquises, lambs for senior ministers, geese for middle ranks, pheasants for minor officials.

sentences.zh: 三公奉璧上殿御坐前，北面。

translations.literal: The three dukes carried discs up the hall before the imperial seat, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Dukes bore jade to the throne facing north.

sentences.zh: 太常贊曰'皇帝為君興'。

translations.literal: The Chamberlain for Ceremonial called: "The emperor rises for his lords."
translations.idiomatic: The Chamberlain intoned that the emperor rose on behalf of his ministers.

sentences.zh: 三公伏。

translations.literal: The three dukes bowed prone.
translations.idiomatic: The three dukes dropped into prostration.

sentences.zh: 皇帝坐，乃前進璧。

translations.literal: When the emperor sat, they advanced with the discs.
translations.idiomatic: Once seated, he allowed them to bring the discs forward.

sentences.zh: 百官皆賀，二千石以上上殿稱萬歲，舉觴，禦食，司徒奉羹，大司農奉飯，奏食舉之樂。

translations.literal: All officials congratulated him; those at two thousand shi and above mounted the hall shouting "long life"; they raised cups; imperial fare was served; the minister of education presented stew and the minister of agriculture rice while the banquet music played.
translations.idiomatic: Two-thousand-shi officers mounted to hail long life, toast, and share imperial food as education and agriculture ministers served broth and grain amid banquet music.

sentences.zh: 百官受賜，宴饗，大作樂，如元正之儀。

translations.literal: The hundred officials received gifts, feasted, and enjoyed full orchestral music like the New Year's observance.
translations.idiomatic: Every rank received largesse and banqueted with full ensembles as on New Year's Day.

sentences.zh: 魏晉則冬至日受方國及百僚稱賀，因小會。

translations.literal: Under Wei and Jin they observed the winter solstice by accepting congratulations from the regions and the bureaucracy and holding a minor gathering.
translations.idiomatic: Wei–Jin courts welcomed regional and bureaucratic homage on the winter solstice with a scaled-down feast.

sentences.zh: 其儀亞於獻歲之旦。

translations.literal: The ceremony ranked just below that of New Year's morning.
translations.idiomatic: Its ritual stood a notch below the first dawn of the year.

sentences.zh: 及武帝泰始四年，詔刺史二千石長吏曰：「古之王者，以歲時巡狩方嶽，其次則二伯述職，不然則行人順省。

translations.literal: By Emperor Wu's fourth Taishi year an edict addressed inspectors and two-thousand-shi senior clerks: "Ancient kings toured the quarterlands by season; next came the two overseers reporting duty; failing that, envoys made orderly inspections.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi 4 Emperor Wu instructed provincial inspectors and county heads: "Antiquity's kings toured the four directions; failing that, twin overseers reported in person; otherwise messengers inspected in due course."

sentences.zh: 故雖幽遐側微，心無壅隔，下情上通，上指遠諭，至於鰥寡，罔不得所，用垂風遺烈，休聲猶存。

translations.literal: Thus even remote and humble regions felt no blockage between high and low; sentiment rose and commands penetrated; down to widowers and widows none lacked their proper place—such exemplary customs left their fragrance and their fair renown still survives.
translations.idiomatic: Distance never cut off communication; policy reached from throne to hovel so even widowed commoners had relief—virtuous governance left echoes still heard.

sentences.zh: 朕在位累載，如臨深川，夙興夕惕，明發不寢，坐而待旦，思四方水旱災眚，為之怛然。

translations.literal: During the years I have occupied the throne it has been like standing beside a deep gorge; I rise early and retire anxious, wake before dawn and cannot sleep, sit awaiting daylight, and ponder flood, drought, and calamity in the four quarters until my heart aches.
translations.idiomatic: Since taking the throne I have lived as one beside a precipice—sleepless before dawn, brooding over drought and flood until grief grips me.

sentences.zh: 勤躬約己，欲令事事當宜。

translations.literal: With diligent self-discipline and restraint I wish every affair to be rightly ordered.
translations.idiomatic: I have tightened my own conduct, striving to set each matter right.

sentences.zh: 常恐眾吏用情，誠心未著，萬機兼猥，慮有不周，政刑失謬，而弗獲備覽。

translations.literal: Yet I constantly fear that officials indulge private feeling, that sincere devotion does not show forth, that myriad affairs pile up disorderly, that care may prove incomplete, that governance and punishments may err, and that I cannot survey everything.
translations.idiomatic: Still I dread clerks acting from favor, honest intent unseen, business piling up faster than judgment, policy or penal justice slipping past review.

sentences.zh: 百姓有過，在予一人。

translations.literal: If the common people err, the fault lies on me alone.
translations.idiomatic: Any fault among the people rests on my person alone.

sentences.zh: 惟歲之不易，未遑卜征巡省之事，下之未乂，其何以恤之。

translations.literal: Only because the year has been hard have I had no leisure for divining expeditions or touring inspections; with the lower realm still unrestful, how am I to bring them relief?
translations.idiomatic: These troubled seasons leave no room for royal tours; while the realm stays unsettled, how may I comfort it?

sentences.zh: 今使使持節侍中副給事黃門侍郎銜命四出，周行天下，親見刺史二千石長吏，申諭朕心，訪求得失損益諸宜，觀省政教，問人間患苦。

translations.literal: Now I dispatch credential-bearing palace attendants and deputy supervisors of the Yellow Gates with commissions to the four quarters to circuit the realm, personally interview inspectors, two-thousand-shi officers, and senior clerks, explain my heart to them, inquire after what should be changed or improved, observe administration and instruction, and ask after human hardship.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore send high envoys to every circuit to meet governors and magistrates in person, convey my intentions, solicit advice on reform, watch how government and education fare, and hear popular grievance.

sentences.zh: 周典有之曰：'其萬姓之利害為一書，其禮俗政事刑禁之逆順為一書，其暴亂作慝犯令為一書，其劄喪凶荒厄貧為一書，其康樂和親安平為一書，每國辨異之，以返命于王。

translations.literal: The Zhou canon states: 'They made one record of benefit and harm to the myriad clans; one of ritual, custom, governance, and whether punishments ran with or against order; one of violence, turmoil, treachery, and violations of command; one of epidemics, mourning, famine, hardship, and destitution; one of health, harmony, kinship, and peace; each state distinguished these differences and reported back to the king.'
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou required separate registers—for popular welfare, for law and custom, for rebellion, for disaster, for prosperity—and each domain distinguished them before reporting to the throne.

sentences.zh: '舊章前訓，今率由之。

translations.literal: 'Ancient statutes and former instructions—now follow them in full."
translations.idiomatic: Those precedents are the model we must follow.

sentences.zh: 還具條奏，俾朕昭然鑒於幽遠，若親行焉。

translations.literal: When you return, set everything forth in memorials so that I may clearly perceive what lies far away as though I had gone myself.
translations.idiomatic: Return with thorough memorials so distant conditions shine before me as if I had walked there.

sentences.zh: 大夫君子，其各悉乃心，敬乃事，嘉言令圖，苦言至戒，與使者盡之，無所隱諱。

translations.literal: Great officers and gentlemen: each pour out your hearts, reverently discharge your duties; welcome counsel and fair designs, heed bitter advice and stern warnings—lay everything before the envoys with nothing concealed.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers: speak plainly—praise sound plans, endure blunt rebuke—and hide nothing from these inspectors.

sentences.zh: 方將慮心以俟，其勉哉勖之，稱朕意焉。」

translations.literal: I shall await you with open mind; exert yourselves and encourage one another; satisfy my intent."
translations.idiomatic: I await your reports with an open heart—strive together until my purpose is met."

sentences.zh: 新禮，巡狩方岳，柴望告設壝宮如禮。

translations.literal: The new ritual for touring the sacred peaks prescribes the mound-altar, blade-fire offerings, and announcements at the circumambulatory palace according to canon.
translations.idiomatic: Revised liturgy for imperial tours mandates ring-wall shrines, burnt offerings, and proclamations as classical precedent demands.

sentences.zh: 諸侯之覲者，賓及執贄皆如朝儀，而不建旗。

translations.literal: When feudatories come to audience, guest reception and tribute-bearing follow court ritual, but they do not raise their banners.
translations.idiomatic: Feudal lords arriving for audience observe gift protocol like inner courtiers yet leave command banners furled.

sentences.zh: 摯虞以為：「覲禮，諸侯覲天子，各建其旗。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu argued: 'Under audience ritual each feudal lord who visits the Son of Heaven erects his own banner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu protested that canonical audience law required every lord to display his standard.

sentences.zh: 旗章所以殊爵命，示等威。

translations.literal: Banners and insignia distinguish invested rank and display hierarchical awe."
translations.idiomatic: Flags mark enfeoffed dignity and visible precedence.

sentences.zh: 《詩》稱'君子至止，言觀其旗'。

translations.literal: The Classic of Poetry says, "When the nobleman arrived, one looked upon his banners."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Songs reads: "The prince had come—note his fluttering flags."

sentences.zh: 宜定新禮，建旗如舊禮。

translations.literal: The new ritual ought to fix banner protocol like the old ritual."
translations.idiomatic: The revised code should restore flag display as antiquity prescribed.

sentences.zh: 」詔可其議。

translations.literal: An edict approved his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor endorsed his memorial.

sentences.zh: 然終晉代，其禮不行。

translations.literal: Yet through the entire Jin age the practice was never carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Nevertheless Jin never actually performed it.

sentences.zh: 封禪之說，經典無聞。

translations.literal: Discourses on feng and shan sacrifices find no mention in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Classical texts never discuss the paired Mount Tai liturgy later called feng and shan.

sentences.zh: 禮有因天事天，因地事地，因名山升中於天，而鳳皇降，龜龍格。

translations.literal: Ritual teaches serving Heaven through Heaven's agencies and Earth through Earth's; ascending a famous peak to report fulfillment to Heaven brings phoenix down and tortoise-dragon to attend.
translations.idiomatic: Canon bids worshipping Heaven via celestial signs and Earth via terrestrial ones; announcing merit atop a sacred summit summons auspicious birds and dragons.

sentences.zh: 天子所以巡狩，至於方岳，燔柴祭天，以告其成功，事似而非也。

translations.literal: This resembles why the Son of Heaven tours to the quarter-peaks, burns kindling to Heaven, and declares success—similar in appearance yet not the same thing.
translations.idiomatic: It looks like the emperor's seasonal march to the directional peaks to burn offerings and report victory, but it is not identical.

sentences.zh: 讖緯諸說皆云，王者封泰山，禪梁甫，易姓紀號。

translations.literal: Prophetic weft texts all declare that kings who feng Mount Tai and shan Mount Liangfu change the dynasty's surname and era.
translations.idiomatic: Apocryphal "weft" writings insist that kings who ascend Tai for feng and Liangfu for shan rename the ruling house.

sentences.zh: 秦漢行其典，前史各陳其制矣。

translations.literal: Qin and Han performed those rites; earlier histories each recorded their forms.
translations.idiomatic: Qin and Han enacted them; earlier annals spell out the choreography.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初中，護軍蔣濟奏曰：「夫帝王大禮，巡狩為先；

translations.literal: During Wei Emperor Wen's Huangchu reign, Household Guards commander Jiang Ji memorialized: 'Among great imperial ceremonies touring inspection comes first;
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu of Wei, Jiang Ji of the Guards wrote: "Of imperial observances, royal tours take pride of place;

sentences.zh: 昭祖揚禰，封禪為首。

translations.literal: to glorify ancestors and extol fathers, feng and shan stand foremost.
translations.idiomatic: to honor forebears and elevate recent fathers, nothing surpasses feng-shan.

sentences.zh: 是以自古革命受符，未有不蹈梁父，登泰山，刊無竟之名，紀天人之際者也。

translations.literal: Hence since antiquity every revolution receiving the celestial tally has climbed Liangfu and ascended Tai, carving inexhaustible fame and recording the conjunction of Heaven and man."
translations.idiomatic: Thus every founding sovereign who received the mandate has climbed Liangfu and Tai to cut everlasting titles into stone and seal Heaven's compact with earth."

sentences.zh: 故司馬相如謂有文以來，七十二君，或順所繇於前，謹遺教於後。

translations.literal: Therefore Sima Xiangru said that since writing appeared seventy-two rulers have done so—some continuing paths opened earlier, some reverently transmitting teaching to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiangru reckoned seventy-two such sovereigns since script began—some continuing roads their predecessors traced, some handing stern lessons to successors.

sentences.zh: 太史公曰，主上有聖明而不宣佈，有司之過也。

translations.literal: The Grand Historian remarked that when the sovereign possesses sagely brilliance yet fails to proclaim it, the blame lies with his ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qian added that keeping sage virtue silent is official negligence.

sentences.zh: 然則元功懿德，不刊梁山之石，無以顯帝王之功，示兆庶不朽之觀也。

translations.literal: Thus supreme merit and lofty virtue, unless inscribed on Liang Mountain stone, cannot display an emperor's achievement or show the myriad households an immortal spectacle.
translations.idiomatic: Without engraving Liangshan, supreme deeds leave no monument for the people to remember.

sentences.zh: 語曰，'當君而歎堯舜之美，譬猶人子對厥所生而譽他人之父'。

translations.literal: A saying runs: "For the ruler to sigh over Yao and Shun's glory is like a son praising another man's father before his own parent."
translations.idiomatic: Proverb warns: praising Yao and Shun while serving one's lord compares to extolling a stranger's father in one's parent's presence.

sentences.zh: 今大魏承百王之弊亂，拯流遁之艱厄，接千載之衰緒，繼百代之廢業。

translations.literal: Now Great Wei inherits the ruin left by a hundred kings, rescues those adrift in peril, takes up a thousand-year thread of decay, and continues enterprises abandoned through endless generations.
translations.idiomatic: Wei arose amid the wreckage of centuries, saving fugitives, repairing a millennium of fracture, restoring abandoned royal work.

sentences.zh: 始自武文，至於聖躬，所以參成天地之道，綱維人神之化。

translations.literal: Beginning with the martial and literary founders down to Your Sagely Person, you have joined Heaven and Earth in pattern and ordered the transformation of gods and men.
translations.idiomatic: From Wudi and Wendi to yourself you have harmonized cosmic pattern and directed spiritual transformation.

sentences.zh: 上天報應，嘉瑞顯祥，以比往古，無所取喻。

translations.literal: Heaven answers with rewards; auspicious omens shine forth—set beside antiquity there is no adequate comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven replies with prodigies no past age can match.

sentences.zh: 至於曆世迄今，未廢大禮。

translations.literal: Yet down to the present generation the grand ceremony has still not been observed.
translations.idiomatic: Still the supreme rite awaits performance.

sentences.zh: 雖志在掃盡殘盜，蕩滌餘穢，未遑斯事。

translations.literal: Although our intent is to sweep away remnant brigands and cleanse lingering filth, there has been no leisure for this affair.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigns against lingering rebels have left no interval.

sentences.zh: 若爾，三苗屈強于江海，大舜當廢東巡之儀；

translations.literal: Were it otherwise, because San Miao stubbornly resisted along the Yangzi regions, Da Shun ought to have abolished eastern tours;
translations.idiomatic: If turmoil forbade ritual, Shun should have canceled eastern progresses while San Miao defied the Yangzi;

sentences.zh: 徐夷跳梁於淮泗，周成當止岱嶽之禮。

translations.literal: because the Xu barbarians leaped about along Huai and Si, King Cheng ought to have halted observances at sacred Dai.
translations.idiomatic: and King Cheng should have skipped Dai peak while Xu raiders thrashed the Huai.

sentences.zh: 且去歲破吳虜于江漢，今茲屠蜀賊於隴右，其震盪內潰，在不復淹，無累于封禪之事也。

translations.literal: Moreover last year we shattered Wu's rebels along the Han rivers and this year butchered Shu bandits west of Long—young trembling collapse will not drag on and cannot obstruct feng-shan.
translations.idiomatic: Last year's victory on the Yangzi and this year's slaughter west of Long mean enemy turmoil ends quickly—nothing blocks the Tai ceremony.

sentences.zh: 此儀久廢，非倉卒所定。

translations.literal: This observance has long lapsed and cannot be fixed overnight.
translations.idiomatic: Long neglect means instant revival is impossible.

sentences.zh: 宜下公卿，廣撰其禮，卜年考時，昭告上帝，以副天下之望。

translations.literal: It should be referred to the dukes and ministers broadly to draft ritual, divine an auspicious year and moment, announce it to High Heaven, and answer all-under-heaven's expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Commission the high ministers to compose liturgy, choose an auspicious season, proclaim intent to Heaven, and satisfy popular hope.

sentences.zh: 臣待罪軍旅，不勝大願，冒死以聞。

translations.literal: Your servant, stationed among the armies, cannot contain his utmost desire and risks death to bring this forward.
translations.idiomatic: I stand guilty amid the hosts yet dare speak though death threaten.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「聞蔣濟斯言，使吾汗出流足。

translations.literal: The edict replied: 'Hearing Jiang Ji's words makes sweat pour down my shanks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered: "Jiang Ji's speech leaves my legs streaming sweat.

sentences.zh: 自開闢以來，封禪者七十餘君耳。

translations.literal: Since creation fewer than seventy rulers have performed feng-shan."
translations.idiomatic: Fewer than seventy sovereigns since time began have mounted Tai."

sentences.zh: 故太史公曰，雖有受命之君，而功有不洽，是以中間曠遠者千有餘年，近者數百載，其儀闕不可得記。

translations.literal: Thus the Grand Historian said that although rulers receive the mandate, merit sometimes stays incomplete—so middle intervals stretch over a thousand years or several hundred while protocols vanish unrecorded.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qian noted that unfinished virtue leaves centuries blank between performances whose forms are lost.

sentences.zh: 吾何德之修，敢庶茲乎！

translations.literal: What virtue have I cultivated that I dare aspire to this!
translations.idiomatic: What virtue could justify my aspiring to join them!

sentences.zh: 濟豈謂世無管仲，以吾有桓公登泰山之志乎！

translations.literal: Does Ji imagine no Guan Zhong survives today and that I harbor Duke Huan's ambition to climb Tai!
translations.idiomatic: Does he think no Guan Zhong restrains me while I secretly imitate Duke Huan's summit?

sentences.zh: 吾不欺天也。

translations.literal: I would not deceive Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I refuse to lie to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 濟之所言，華則華矣，非助我者也。

translations.literal: What Ji says is fluent rhetoric, not counsel that helps me.
translations.idiomatic: His prose dazzles but offers no aid.

sentences.zh: 公卿侍中尚書常侍省之而已，勿復有所議，亦不須答詔也。

translations.literal: Let the dukes, ministers, attendants, secretariat directors, and regular attendants review it among themselves—need offer no further debate, nor reply by edict."
translations.idiomatic: House it among ministers for reference—debate ends; no answering decree required."

sentences.zh: 」天子雖距濟議，而實使高堂隆草封禪之儀，以天下未一，不欲便行大禮，會隆卒，不復行之。

translations.literal: Although the Son of Heaven rejected Jiang's plea, he secretly ordered Gao Tang Long to draft feng-shan protocol; because the realm was not yet unified he hesitated to enact the grand rite—when Long died the matter lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The throne refused Jiang Ji yet quietly had Gao Tang Long draft liturgy; reluctant while China stayed divided, it abandoned the plan when Long died.

sentences.zh: 及武帝平吳，混一區宇，太康元年九月庚寅，尚書令衛瓘、尚書左僕射山濤、右僕射魏舒、尚書劉寔、司空張華等奏曰：「臣聞肇自生靈，則有後辟，年載之數，莫之能紀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu pacified Wu and unified the realm, on gengyin day in the ninth month of Taikang year one, Minister Director Wei Guan, Left Director Shan Tao, Right Director Wei Shu, Minister Liu Shi, Minister of Works Zhang Hua, and others memorialized: 'We have heard that ever since living beings arose there have been later sovereigns, yet years beyond counting cannot be tallied.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu fell, on Taikang 1/IX/gengyin Wei Guan, Shan Tao, Wei Shu, Liu Shi, Zhang Hua wrote: "Since humanity began rulers have succeeded beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 立德濟世，揮揚仁風，以登封泰山者七十有四家，其諡號可知者十有四焉。

translations.literal: Those who established virtue to aid the age and spread humane influence, ascending Tai to report completion, number seventy-four houses; only fourteen posthumous titles can still be known.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-four dynasts reportedly mounted Tai with humane sway; fourteen names survive.

sentences.zh: 沈淪寂寞，曾無遺聲者，不可勝記。

translations.literal: Those sunk in oblivion without surviving fame cannot be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Countless others sank mute into oblivion.

sentences.zh: 大晉之德，始自重黎，實佐顓頊，至於夏商，世序天地。

translations.literal: Great Jin's virtue begins with Chong Li, who truly aided Zhuanxu; down through Xia and Yin they sequenced Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Our mandate traces to Chong Li aiding Zhuanxu; Xia and Shang heirs ordered cosmos and soil.

sentences.zh: 其在於周，不失其緒。

translations.literal: Under the Zhou house they never lost that thread.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou continued that lineage unbroken.

sentences.zh: 金德將升，世濟明聖，外平蜀漢，海內歸心，武功之盛，實由文德。

translations.literal: When the golden virtue was about to arise, generation upon generation produced enlightened sages; they pacified Shu-Han abroad and won hearts within—the martial triumph truly stemmed from civil virtue.
translations.idiomatic: As Jin's golden virtue rose, sage kings multiplied; conquering Shu abroad while winning hearts at home proved arms rested on culture.

sentences.zh: 至於陛下，受命踐阼，弘建大業，群生仰流。

translations.literal: Coming to Your Majesty: receiving the mandate and ascending the throne, you enlarge the great enterprise as all living beings look upward.
translations.idiomatic: You took the throne and expanded the enterprise while creation lifts its eyes.

sentences.zh: 惟獨江湖沅湘之表，凶桀負固，歷代不賓。

translations.literal: Only beyond the Yangzi along Yuan and Xiang, vicious brutes clung to strongholds and refused tribute through successive reigns.
translations.idiomatic: Only south of the great rivers did rebels cling to fastnesses age after age.

sentences.zh: 神謀獨斷，命將出討，兵威暫加，數旬蕩定。

translations.literal: By singular stratagem you ordered generals forth; martial majesty struck briefly and within weeks they were swept away.
translations.idiomatic: Your decisive orders sent armies whose shock pacified them within tens of days.

sentences.zh: 羈其鯨鯢，赦其罪逆，雲覆雨施，八方來同，聲教所被，達於四極。

translations.literal: You bound their chief rebels yet pardoned guilty remnants; favor fell like cloud-borne rain until eight directions converged and cultural influence reached the four limits.
translations.idiomatic: You shackled ringleaders yet forgave followers; grace spread like rain until every quarter submitted and civilization touched the rim.

sentences.zh: 雖黃軒遐征，大禹遠略，周之奕世，何以尚今！

translations.literal: Though the Yellow Emperor marched far or Yu surveyed distant wastes or Zhou prospered through generations—what could surpass today!
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Emperor's distant march, Great Yu's far planning, Zhou's long prosperity—none outshine this.

sentences.zh: 若夫玄石素文，底號前載，象以數表，言以事告，雖古《河圖洛書》之徵，不是過也。

translations.literal: As for black stones bearing pale script, titles proclaimed in earlier records, figures shown by numerology, events foretold in words—even ancient signs of the Yellow River chart and Luo River writing do not surpass them.
translations.idiomatic: Dark stones with pale inscriptions, titled omens, numbered images, verbal prophecies—these eclipse even Hetu and Luoshu.

sentences.zh: 宜宣大典，禮中嶽，封泰山，禪梁父，發德號，明至尊，享天休，篤黎庶，勒千載之表，播流後之聲，俾百世之下，莫不興起。

translations.literal: You ought to proclaim the great canon, sacrifice at central peak, feng Mount Tai, shan Mount Liangfu, issue virtue titles, clarify supremacy, enjoy Heaven's rest, enrich the black-haired people, carve a millennium's monument, broadcast fame to posterity, so that a hundred generations hence all take fire from your example.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore enact the grand ceremony: worship the sacred median, feng Tai, shan Liangfu, proclaim virtue, manifest supremacy, receive Heaven's grace, enrich the people, and engrave fame for ages.

sentences.zh: 斯帝王之盛業，天人之至望也。

translations.literal: Such is an emperor's crowning achievement and Heaven-and-man's utmost hope."
translations.idiomatic: This crowns imperial duty and fulfills cosmic expectation."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「今逋寇雖殄，外則障塞有警，內則百姓未甯，此盛德之事，所未議也。」

translations.literal: The edict answered: 'Though fleeing bandits are destroyed, outwardly the frontier alarms and inwardly the hundred clans lack tranquillity—such matters of supreme virtue are not yet for discussion.'
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Remnant foes die yet borders bristle and folk remain restless—this supreme deed stays premature."

sentences.zh: 瓘等又奏曰：「今東漸於海，西被流沙，大漠之陰，日南北戶，莫不通屬，芒芒禹跡，今實過之。

translations.literal: Wei Guan and colleagues memorialized again: 'Now influence reaches eastward to the sea, spreads west across drifting sands, north beyond the great desert, south to sun-facing doors—nothing lies outside allegiance; Yu's vast footprints are truly surpassed.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed on: "Our sway washes to the eastern sea, spans western sands, crosses the desert's northern rim and southern tropics—Yu the Great's realm is smaller.

sentences.zh: 天人之道已周，巍巍之功已著，宜修禮地祗，登封泰山，致誠上帝，以答人神之願也。

translations.literal: Heaven-and-man's Way is complete; towering merit shines forth—you should cultivate ritual to Earth gods, ascend Tai in feng, show utmost sincerity to High Heaven, answering gods' and men's prayers.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's circuit closes; glory towers—worship terrestrial spirits, scale Tai, declare sincerity to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 乞如前奏。

translations.literal: We beg permission as before."
translations.idiomatic: We renew our plea."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「今陰陽未和，刑政未當，百姓未得其所，豈可以勒功告成邪！

translations.literal: The edict replied: 'Yin and yang are not yet harmonious, punishments and governance not yet fitting, the hundred clans have not found their places—how could we carve merit and proclaim completion!'
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Omens stay discordant, law imperfect, people unsettled—how dare we boast completion!

sentences.zh: 」詔不許。

translations.literal: The edict refused.
translations.idiomatic: He denied them.

sentences.zh: 瓘等又奏曰：「臣聞處帝王之位者，必有曆運之期，天命之應；

translations.literal: Wei Guan and others memorialized again: 'We have heard that whoever occupies the imperial seat must meet the epoch's turning and Heaven's response;
translations.idiomatic: They wrote again: "Throne holders face ordained seasons and celestial confirmation;

sentences.zh: 濟兆庶之功者，必有盛德之容，告成之典。

translations.literal: whoever delivers the myriad people must possess majestic virtue's bearing and the canon of declaring achievement.
translations.idiomatic: deliverers of the masses display august deportment and victory liturgy.

sentences.zh: 無不可誣，有不敢讓，自古道也。

translations.literal: Nothing may be fabricated; possession cannot be declined—the Way has always been thus.
translations.idiomatic: Truth cannot be feigned; possession cannot be refused—such is antiquity.

sentences.zh: 而明詔謙沖，屢辭其禮，雖盛德攸在，推而未居。

translations.literal: Yet enlightened edicts stay modest, repeatedly declining this ritual; although supreme virtue abides, you push forward yet do not assume it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet humble decrees refuse the rite though virtue warrants it.

sentences.zh: 夫三公職典天地，實掌人物，國之大事，取議於此。

translations.literal: The three dukes administer Heaven and Earth and truly manage human affairs—great matters of state are deliberated there.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Dukes harmonize cosmos and humanity—state crises land on their benches.

sentences.zh: 故漢氏封禪，非是官也，不在其事。

translations.literal: Thus Han-dynasty feng-shan did not involve these offices—they did not handle the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Han conducted feng-shan without them—they lacked jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 臣等前奏，蓋陳祖考之功，天命又應，陛下之德，合同四海，跡古考今，宜修此禮。

translations.literal: Our earlier memorial outlined ancestral merit, Heaven's response, and Your Majesty's virtue harmonizing the four seas; scanning past and present you should restore this observance.
translations.idiomatic: We cited ancestors, omens, and your virtue binding the seas—history demands renewal.

sentences.zh: 至於克定歲月，須五府上議，然後奏聞。

translations.literal: As for fixing the calendar date, let the five ministries propose jointly, then memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: Choose the season after joint deliberation among the five boards.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「雖蕩清江表，皆臨事者之勞，何足以告成。

translations.literal: The edict replied: 'Though the Yangzi region is pacified, that is merely the labor of commanders on the scene—how does it suffice to declare completion?
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Southern pacification credits field officers alone.

sentences.zh: 方望群後思隆大化，以甯區夏，百姓獲乂，與之休息。

translations.literal: I look to the regional lords together to broaden transformation so the central realm may rest and the hundred clans gain peace—share repose with them.
translations.idiomatic: I await governors to spread transformation until the heartland calms and people recover.

sentences.zh: 斯朕日夜之望，無所復下諸府矣。」

translations.literal: This is my nightly hope; refer it no further to the ministries."
translations.idiomatic: Send nothing more to the boards."

sentences.zh: 瓘等又奏：「臣聞唐虞三代濟世弘功之君，莫不仰承天休，俯協人志，登介丘，履梁父，未有辭焉者，蓋不可讓也。

translations.literal: Wei Guan and others memorialized: 'We have heard that sagely rulers from Tang, Yu, and the Three Ages who aided the age with vast merit invariably received Heaven's blessing, coordinated human aspiration, climbed lesser peaks, trod Liangfu—none declined, for refusal was impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: They argued: "Tang-Yu exemplars who saved the world accepted Heaven's gift, climbed sacred heights—decline was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 今陛下勳高百王，德無與二，茂績宏規，巍巍之業，固非臣等所能究論。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty's merit towers over a hundred kings; virtue finds no second; glorious deeds and grand model—the lofty enterprise—is truly beyond our words.
translations.idiomatic: Your feats overshadow every ruler; virtue stands peerless beyond our praise.

sentences.zh: 而聖旨勞謙，屢自抑損，時至弗應，推美不居，闕皇代之上儀，塞靈祗之款望，何以使大晉之典謨，同風於三五？

translations.literal: Yet sagely intent labors in humility, repeatedly restraining itself; the moment arrives yet goes unanswered, merit is deferred—the supreme observance of our august age gaps while numinous powers wait longing—how may Great Jin's charter rival the Three Augusts and Five Emperors?
translations.idiomatic: Yet modest edicts stall heaven-sent timing and frustrate spirits—how can Jin match the legendary Five?

sentences.zh: 臣等誠不敢奉詔，請如前奏施行。

translations.literal: We truly dare not obey the edict; beg to enact our earlier memorial.
translations.idiomatic: We cannot obey silence—grant the earlier plan.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「方當共思弘道，以康庶績，且俟他年，無所復紛紜也。」

translations.literal: The edict replied: 'We shall jointly ponder enlarging the Way to secure myriad accomplishments—wait for another year; debate ends here.'
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Let us broaden the Mandate first—defer another year; no more memorials."

sentences.zh: 王公有司又奏：「自古聖明，光宅四海，封禪名山，著于史籍，作者七十四君矣。

translations.literal: Royal dukes and responsible offices memorialized: 'Since antiquity enlightened sages illumining the four seas and feng-shan on famous peaks appear in annals—seventy-four rulers have performed them.
translations.idiomatic: The nobility wrote: "Seventy-four luminous sovereigns lit the realm and carved Tai—history records each.

sentences.zh: 舜禹之有天下也，巡狩四嶽，躬行其道。

translations.literal: When Shun and Yu possessed All-under-heaven they toured the four peaks and personally enacted the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Shun and Yu toured the directional peaks enacting the Dao.

sentences.zh: 《易》著觀俗省方，《禮》有升中於天，《詩》頌陟其高山，皆載在方策。

translations.literal: The Changes discusses observing customs and inspecting regions; the Rites speaks of ascending to report to Heaven; the Poetry hymns climbing lofty mountains—all stand inscribed on bamboo and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Zhouyi praises inspection tours; Rites mandates summit reports; Songs celebrate mountain ascent—all canonical.

sentences.zh: 文王為西伯以服事殷，周公以魯籓列于諸侯，或享於岐山，或有事泰山，徒以聖德，猶得為其事。

translations.literal: King Wen served Yin as western lord; Duke Dan's Lu enfeoffment ranked among feudatories—yet one sacrificed at Mount Qi, another performed business at Tai—purely through sagely virtue they could handle such affairs.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen served Shang yet sacrificed at Qi; Duke of Zhou's Lu still offered at Tai—sage virtue alone justified it.

sentences.zh: 自是以來，功薄而僭其義者，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Since then those whose merit was thin yet usurped the meaning cannot be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Petty usurpers who mimicked the rite swarm beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 號諡不泯，以至於今。

translations.literal: Titles and posthumous names were never erased down to today.
translations.idiomatic: Their boasts survive in epithets.

sentences.zh: 況高祖宣皇帝肇開王業，海外有截；

translations.literal: Moreover Gaozu Xuan Emperor opened the royal enterprise and beyond the seas submitted;
translations.idiomatic: Our dynastic grandfather Xuan opened kingship and coastal realms bent;

sentences.zh: 世宗景皇帝濟以大功，輯甯區夏；

translations.literal: Shizong Jing Emperor aided it with great merit and settled the central realm;
translations.idiomatic: Jing Emperor restored peace to the heartland;

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝受命造晉，蕩定蜀漢；

translations.literal: Taizu Wen Emperor received the mandate founding Jin and eradicated Shu-Han;
translations.idiomatic: Wen Emperor founded Jin and crushed Shu;

sentences.zh: 陛下應期龍興，混一六合，澤被群生，威震無外。

translations.literal: Your Majesty answered the epoch's dragon ascent, unified the six directions, spread kindness over creation, and awed all beyond reach.
translations.idiomatic: You rose with the hour, reunified the realm, showered grace, and terrified none left outside.

sentences.zh: 昔漢氏失統，吳蜀鼎峙，兵興以來，近將百年，地險俗殊，人望絕塞。

translations.literal: Formerly Han lost unity while Wu and Shu stood tripod-wise; since armies marched nearly a hundred years have passed—terrain perilous, customs alien, popular hopes cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Han collapse split Wu and Shu; a century of war estranged peoples across brutal terrain.

sentences.zh: 今不羈之寇，二代而平，非聰明神武，先天弗違，孰能巍巍其有成功若茲者歟！

translations.literal: Now unrestrained foes fell within two reigns—unless intelligence and divine martial prowess matched Heaven beforehand, who could achieve such towering success!
translations.idiomatic: Yet incorrigible enemies vanished within two reigns—without Heaven-guided genius who could succeed so grandly!

sentences.zh: 臣等幸以千載得遭運會，親服大化，目睹太平，至公至美，誰與為讓。

translations.literal: We have been fortunate through this millennium to meet the cosmic conjunction, personally submit to great transformation, witness universal peace—supreme impartiality and supreme beauty admit no yielding.
translations.idiomatic: We live once in an age of universal peace—such completeness leaves no room for modest refusal.

sentences.zh: 宜祖述先朝，憲章古昔，勒功岱岳，登封告成，弘禮樂之制，正三雍之典，揚名萬世，以顯祖宗。

translations.literal: You ought to take former courts as models, take statutes from antiquity, carve merit at sacred Dai, ascend Tai to declare completion, enlarge ritual and music's institutions, rectify the three Yong academy's canons, spread fame ten thousand generations, and manifest ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Follow founding precedents and classical models: report victory at Tai, institute ritual music, fix the Three Yong curriculum, and glorify the ancestral shrine for ages.

sentences.zh: 是以不勝大願，敢昧死以聞。

translations.literal: Therefore, unable to contain our utmost desire, we dare risk death to bring this forward.
translations.idiomatic: We speak though death threaten, so urgent is our hope.

sentences.zh: 請告太常，具禮儀復上。

translations.literal: We ask that the Chamberlain for Ceremonial be notified to prepare full protocols and memorialize again.
translations.idiomatic: Charge the Chamberlain for Ceremonial to draft liturgy and resubmit.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「所議誠列代之盛事也，然方今未可以爾。

translations.literal: The edict replied: 'What you discuss is truly a splendid affair of successive ages, yet presently we may not do thus.'
translations.idiomatic: The throne answered: "Your topic marks every dynasty's summit—but not yet our season."

sentences.zh: 」便報絕之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the reply cut them off.
translations.idiomatic: With that the court closed discussion.

sentences.zh: 哀帝即位，欲尊崇章皇太妃。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ai assumed the throne he wished to honor Imperial Consort Zhang as senior imperial mother.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ai sought higher honors for Consort Zhang, his birth mother.

sentences.zh: 桓溫議宜稱太夫人。

translations.literal: Huan Wen argued she should be titled Grand Lady (太夫人).
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen preferred the style "Grand Lady."

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射江虨議曰：「虞舜體仁孝之性，盡事親之禮，貴為天王，富有四海，而瞽叟無立錐之地，一級之爵。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat Jiang Bin argued: 'Shun embodied humane filial nature and exhausted service to kin; though honored as heaven's king and wealthy within the four seas, Blind Gu had no ground for even a cone's point nor one rank's noble title.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Bin cited Shun: enthroned over all yet his blind father lacked land or rank.

sentences.zh: 蒸蒸之心，昊天罔極，甯當忍父卑賤，不以徽號顯之，豈不以子無爵父之道，理窮義屈，靡所厝情者哉！

translations.literal: His mounting affection reached inexhaustibly toward azure Heaven—how could he endure a father's baseness and fail to display him with glorious titles? Was it not because the Way admits no son ennobling father—principle exhausted, duty twisted, nowhere to place affection?"
translations.idiomatic: Could Shun leave his father titleless? Canon forbids sons raising parents—duty stalls, feeling has no outlet.

sentences.zh: 《春秋經》曰'紀季姜歸於京師'，《傳》曰'父母之于子，雖為天王後，猶曰吾季薑'，言子尊不加父母也。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals records "Lady Jiang of Ji returned to the capital"; the commentary says "Parents toward children—even when she becomes heaven's queen—still say 'my Jiang,' meaning a child's honor does not surpass parents."
translations.idiomatic: The Annals line "Lady Jiang of Ji returned" shows parents still say "my little Jiang" though she wed the Son of Heaven—child rank never outranks parents.

sentences.zh: 或以為子尊不加父母，則武王何以追王太王、王季、文王乎？

translations.literal: Some argue if child honor does not surpass parents, why did King Wu posthumously enthrone Taiwang, Wang Ji, and King Wen?
translations.idiomatic: Critics ask how King Wu could king his forebears if sons cannot elevate parents.

sentences.zh: 周之三王，德配天地，王跡之興，自此始也。

translations.literal: Zhou's three kings matched Heaven and Earth in virtue; royal footprints arose from them.
translations.idiomatic: Those three Zhou founders embodied cosmic virtue—the lineage began there.

sentences.zh: 是以武王仰尋前緒，遂奉天命，追崇祖考，明不以子尊加父母也。

translations.literal: Therefore King Wu looked upward along prior threads, obeyed Heaven's mandate, posthumously honored ancestors, clarifying that child honor does not override parents.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu therefore pursued Heaven's charge through honoring ancestors—proving elevation served mandate, not filial inflation.

sentences.zh: 案《禮》'幼不誄長，賤不誄貴'，幼賤猶不得表彰長貴，況敢錫之以榮命邪！

translations.literal: According to the Rites, "the young does not compose elegies for elders, the base does not elegize the noble"—if youth and low rank still may not glorify seniors and superiors, how dare we bestow glittering commissions!
translations.idiomatic: The Rites forbid youths elegizing elders or commoners nobles—much less granting patent splendor upward.

sentences.zh: 漢祖感家令之言而尊太公，荀悅以為孝莫大于嚴父，而以子貴加之父母，家令之言過矣。

translations.literal: Han Founder heeded the household steward's advice and honored Grand Duke Gao; Xun Yue held that nothing surpasses honoring a stern father, yet applying child-noble rank to parents overshoots—the steward's counsel erred.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu elevated his father at a retainer's word; Xun Yue called revering fathers supreme yet warned against grafting son's dignity onto parents.

sentences.zh: 爰逮孝章，不上賈貴人以尊號，而厚其金寶幣帛，非子道之不至也，蓋聖典不可逾也。

translations.literal: Down to Zhangdi he did not elevate Lady Jia with exalted titles but enriched her gold, treasure, cloth, and silk—not that filial devotion fell short but sagely canon cannot be transgressed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han's Zhangdi withheld lofty titles from Lady Jia while enriching her—scripture, not coldness, barred inflation.

sentences.zh: 當春秋時，庶子承國，其母得為夫人。

translations.literal: During Spring and Autumn times when a bastard heir succeeded a state his mother could become principal lady.
translations.idiomatic: When secondary sons inherited states, their mothers sometimes became chief consorts.

sentences.zh: 不審直子命母邪，故當告于宗祧以先君之命命之邪？

translations.literal: Is it unclear whether the legitimate son commanded the mother or whether one should report to the ancestral shrine and use the former lord's mandate to command her?
translations.idiomatic: Did the heir appoint her, or did ancestral decree through the shrine?

sentences.zh: 竊見詔書，當臨軒拜授貴人為皇太妃。

translations.literal: Privately observing the edict, it will face south from the hall to invest the noble lady as imperial dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The decree schedules a formal hall audience investing her as imperial mother.

sentences.zh: 今稱皇帝策命命貴人，斯則子爵母也。

translations.literal: Now if we style it an imperial edict commanding the noble lady, that makes the son grant noble rank to the mother.
translations.idiomatic: Calling it an imperial mandate makes the son the mother's ennobler.

sentences.zh: 貴人北面拜受，斯則母臣子也。

translations.literal: The noble lady bows north receiving investiture—that makes the mother minister to the son.
translations.idiomatic: She would kneel north—mother serving son.

sentences.zh: 天尊地卑，名位定矣，母貴子賤，人倫序矣。

translations.literal: Heaven is honored, earth low—names and positions are fixed; mother noble, child base—human ethics are ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven stands high, earth low—stations settle ethics; reversing mother and son inverts the moral ladder.

sentences.zh: 雖欲加崇貴人，而實卑之；

translations.literal: Although wishing to exalt the noble lady, in truth one debases her;
translations.idiomatic: Grand titles would actually diminish her.

sentences.zh: 雖顯明國典，而實廢之。

translations.literal: although manifestly displaying state statutes, in truth one abolishes them.
translations.idiomatic: Displaying law would nullify it.

sentences.zh: 且人主舉動，史必書之。

translations.literal: Moreover every ruler's act history must record.
translations.idiomatic: Historians inscribe each sovereign gesture.

sentences.zh: 如當載之方策，以示後世，無乃不順乎！

translations.literal: If this entered bamboo documents to show posterity, would it not violate proper order!
translations.idiomatic: Future readers would see a constitutional absurdity.

sentences.zh: 竊謂應告顯宗之廟，稱貴人仁淑之至，宜加殊禮，以酬鞠育之惠。

translations.literal: I privately believe one should announce at Emperor Xianzong's shrine that the noble lady's humane virtue deserves extraordinary observance to repay nurture's kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Better report at Mingdi's temple her nurturing virtue merits special—but indirect—honors.

sentences.zh: 奉先靈之命，事不在己。

translations.literal: Receiving the command of the ancestral spirit, the affair does not rest on oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Attributes honor to the departed emperor's will, not the sitting throne.

sentences.zh: 妃後雖是配君之名，然自後以下有夫人九嬪，無稱妃焉。

translations.literal: Though imperial consorts serve as the ruler's counterpart in name, below empress come ladies and nine concubines—none titled simple "consort."
translations.idiomatic: After empress rank follow ladies-in-waiting—no bare "fei" title.

sentences.zh: 桓公謂宜進號太夫人，非不允也。

translations.literal: Lord Huan said advancing her to Grand Lady was not unacceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen's "Grand Lady" was not unreasonable.

sentences.zh: 如以夫人為少，可言皇太夫人。

translations.literal: If "lady" seems slight, one may say imperial Grand Lady.
translations.idiomatic: If "lady" feels thin, add the imperial prefix.

sentences.zh: 皇，君也，君太夫人于名禮順矣。

translations.literal: Imperial means sovereign; addressing Grand Lady under imperial fits name and ritual.
translations.idiomatic: "Imperial Grand Lady" pairs supremacy with canonical mother styles.

sentences.zh: 」帝特下詔拜皇太妃。

translations.literal: The emperor specially issued edict investing her as imperial honored consort (皇太妃).
translations.idiomatic: The throne overrode debate with the title imperial dowager-consort.

sentences.zh: 三月丙辰，使兼太保王恬授璽綬儀服，一如太后。

translations.literal: On bingchen of the third month he ordered concurrent Junior Tutor Wang Tian to present seals, ribbons, regalia, and garments identical to an empress dowager's.
translations.idiomatic: Third-month bingchen Wang Tian delivered seals and robes matching empress dowager standards.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「朝臣不為太妃敬，為合禮不？

translations.literal: Another edict asked: "Do court ministers owe reverence to the imperial dowager-consort—does ritual require it?"
translations.idiomatic: A follow-up asked whether ministers must bow to her.

sentences.zh: 」太常江逌議：「位號不極，不應盡敬。」

translations.literal: Chamberlain Jiang Yi ruled: "Her station lacks supreme title—she should not receive full reverence."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yi replied that without paramount rank full court bows were improper.

sentences.zh: 孝武追崇會稽鄭太妃為簡文太后，詔問「當開墓不」。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu posthumously honored Kuaiji Lady Zheng as Empress Dowager Jianwen and edicted asking whether to open her tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu elevated Consort Zheng of Kuaiji as Jianwen's empress dowager and queried reopening her grave.

sentences.zh: 王珣答：「據三祖追贈及中宗敬後，並不開墓位，更為塋域制度耳。」

translations.literal: Wang Xun answered: "Judging from the three ancestors' posthumous grants and Middle Ancestor's reverenced empress, none opened tomb sites—they only enlarged mound precinct regulations."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xun cited earlier Jin burials: honorifics added tombs but never reopened chambers.

sentences.zh: 褚太后臨朝時，議褚裒進見之典。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Chu held court they debated Chu Pou's audience protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Chu regency ministers discussed how her father Chu Pou should attend.

sentences.zh: 蔡謨、王彪之並以：「虞舜、漢高祖猶執子道，況後乎！

translations.literal: Cai Mo and Wang Biaozhi jointly argued: 'Even Shun and Han Gaozu still observed son's deportment—how much more later ages!
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo and Wang Biaozhi noted Shun and Gaozu kept filial posture toward elders.

sentences.zh: 王者父無拜禮。

translations.literal: For kings and lords the father performs no bow."
translations.idiomatic: Sovereigns do not bow to fathers.

sentences.zh: 」尚書八座議以為：「純子則王道缺，純臣則孝道虧。

translations.literal: The Eight Seats of the Secretariat ruled: 'Pure sonliness leaves kingship deficient; pure minister leaves filiality lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat heads answered: "Pure family feeling weakens kingship; pure court hierarchy starves piety.

sentences.zh: 謂公庭如臣，私覿則嚴父為允。」

translations.literal: We say in public court behave as ministers; in private meeting honor the stern father—that is fitting."
translations.idiomatic: Public halls demand ministerial bows; private chambers allow parental reverence.

sentences.zh: 漢魏故事，皇太子稱臣。

translations.literal: Han and Wei precedent had the crown prince style himself minister.
translations.idiomatic: Han–Wei custom let the heir apparent call himself "minister."

sentences.zh: 新禮以太子既以子為名，而又稱臣，臣子兼稱，於義不通，除太子稱臣之制。

translations.literal: New ritual argued that because the heir is already named "son," also calling himself minister mixes two relations—meaning conflicts—so remove the crown prince's minister usage.
translations.idiomatic: Revised codes banned the redundant "minister" style for an heir already defined as son.

sentences.zh: 摯虞以為：「《孝經》'資于事父以事君'，義兼臣子，則不嫌稱臣，宜定新禮皇太子稱臣如舊。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu argued: 'The Classic of Filial Piety says "take from serving father the manner of serving lord," combining minister and son—thus no shame in saying minister; new ritual should restore crown prince minister usage like old.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu cited the Filial Piety Classic merging filial and loyal roles—minister language fit and should return.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict followed his opinion.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 太寧三年三月戊辰，明帝立皇子衍為皇太子。

translations.literal: On wuchen in the third month of Taining 3 Emperor Ming established imperial son Yan as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Taining 3/III/wuchen Mingdi named Yan heir.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，詔曰：「禮無生而貴者，故帝元子方之於士。

translations.literal: On guisi an edict stated: 'Ritual admits no innate nobility—therefore the emperor's eldest son matches a common knight.
translations.idiomatic: That month's guisi decree quoted canon: the emperor's firstborn ranks like an ordinary gentleman.

sentences.zh: 而漢魏以來，尊崇儲貳，使官屬稱臣，朝臣咸拜，此甚無謂。

translations.literal: Yet since Han–Wei times they have revered the heir apparent, making his officials address him as minister while courtiers all bow—deeply pointless.
translations.idiomatic: Han–Wei fashion overrated the heir: household styled him lord while everyone bowed—senseless.

sentences.zh: 吾昔在東宮，未及啟革。

translations.literal: Formerly when I dwelt in the Eastern Palace I lacked chance to reform it.
translations.idiomatic: I lived there too briefly to fix it.

sentences.zh: 今衍幼沖之年，便臣先達，將令日習所見，謂之自然，此豈可以教之邪！

translations.literal: Now Yan is still in tender years yet makes elders his ministers—daily habit will deem it natural—how can we instruct him thus!
translations.idiomatic: Young Yan would train seasoned men to kneel—daily sight would mistake subservience for nature.

sentences.zh: 主者其下公卿內外通議，使必允禮中。

translations.literal: Those in charge shall order dukes and ministers inside and out to deliberate jointly until ritual surely hits the mean."
translations.idiomatic: Order thorough debate until observance reaches the golden mean.

sentences.zh: 」尚書令卞壼議以為：「《周禮》王后太子不會，明禮同於君，皆所以重儲貳，異正嫡。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Bian Kun argued: 'The Rites of Zhou says queen and heir do not attend certain assemblies—clearly ritual ranks them with the ruler to emphasize the heir and distinguish legitimate succession.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Kun cited Zhouli exempting queen and heir from some gatherings—they stood parallel to the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 苟奉之如君，不得不拜矣。

translations.literal: If they serve him like the ruler, bowing becomes unavoidable.
translations.idiomatic: Equal dignity compels others to bow.

sentences.zh: 太子若存謙沖，故宜答拜。

translations.literal: Should the heir preserve modesty, returning bows is proper.
translations.idiomatic: He may modestly bow back.

sentences.zh: 臣以為皇太子之立，郊告天地，正位儲宮，豈得同之皇子揖讓而已。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that once the crown prince is established, suburban announcement reaches Heaven and Earth and he occupies the heir's palace—how can he match mere imperial sons exchanging bows?
translations.idiomatic: After suburban proclamation and investiture he outranks ordinary princes' mutual bows.

sentences.zh: 謂宜稽則漢魏，闔朝同拜。

translations.literal: We say follow Han–Wei precedent: whole court bows together."
translations.idiomatic: Restore Han–Wei: universal obeisance.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The throne followed this.
translations.idiomatic: His majesty agreed.

sentences.zh: 太元中，尚書符問王公已下見皇太子儀及所衣服。

translations.literal: During Taiyuan the Secretariat issued directive asking protocol and dress for royal dukes downward when meeting the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan-era boards queried how nobles should dress and bow before the heir.

sentences.zh: 侍中領國子博士車胤議：「朝臣宜硃衣褠幘，拜敬，太子答拜。

translations.literal: Palace attendant and imperial academy supervisor Che Yin argued: 'Court ministers should wear red robes with wrapped turbans, bow reverently, and the heir return bow.
translations.idiomatic: Che Yin prescribed scarlet jackets and turbans with mutual bows.

sentences.zh: 案經傳不見其文，故太傅羊祜箋慶太子，稱叩頭死罪，此則拜之證也。

translations.literal: Canon and commentary do not spell it out, yet Junior Tutor Yang Hu's congratulatory note to the heir read "knocking head, deserving death"—proof bowing obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Texts stay silent, yet Yang Hu's memorial used criminal submission language—evidence of bowing.

sentences.zh: 又太寧三年詔議其典，尚書卞壼謂宜稽則漢魏，闔朝同拜。

translations.literal: Moreover Taining 3's edict debated the canon and Director Bian Kun said follow Han–Wei—whole court bows.
translations.idiomatic: Taining deliberation already chose universal bows per Bian Kun.

sentences.zh: 其硃衣冠冕，惟施之天朝，宜褠幘而已。

translations.literal: Vermilion crowns and court robes belong only to celestial court audiences—here turbans suffice."
translations.idiomatic: Full court crowns suit imperial audiences alone; heir meetings need simpler caps.

sentences.zh: 」朝議多同。

translations.literal: Court debate largely concurred.
translations.idiomatic: Consensus matched.

sentences.zh: 太元十二年，議二王后與太子先後。
