translations.literal: Taiyuan 12 they debated whether the two royal houses or the crown prince went first.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth year of Taiyuan addressed precedence between Han–Wei ritual hosts and the heir.

sentences.zh: 博士庾弘之及尚書參議，並以為：「陳留，國之上賓。

translations.literal: Doctor Yu Hongzhi and Secretariat deliberators jointly held: 'Chenliu ranks as the state's guest of honor.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Hongzhi rated the Chenliu king supreme guest.

sentences.zh: 皇太子雖國之儲貳，猶在臣位，陳留王坐應在太子上。

translations.literal: Though the crown prince is dynastic heir he remains in ministerial station—the Chenliu king's seat should lie above the heir's.
translations.idiomatic: The heir stays "minister" to the symbolic Han line—Chenliu sits higher.

sentences.zh: 」陳留王勱表稱疾病積年，求放罷，詔禮官博士議之。

translations.literal: Chenliu King Li memorialized chronic illness seeking dismissal; the edict ordered ritual doctors to debate.
translations.idiomatic: King Li pleaded sickness and abdication; the throne sought scholarly opinion.

sentences.zh: 博士曹耽云：「勱為祭主而無執祭之期，宜與穆子、孟摯事同。

translations.literal: Doctor Cao Dan said: 'Li serves as sacrifice lord yet lacks scheduled observances—his case matches Mu Zi and Meng Zhi.'
translations.idiomatic: Cao Dan compared him to Mu Zi/Meng Zhi—titular priests without rites.

sentences.zh: 」王彪之云：「二王之後，不宜輕致廢立。

translations.literal: Wang Biaozhi said: 'Scions of the two royal houses should not lightly face deposition.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biaozhi warned against casually removing charter kings.

sentences.zh: 記傳未見有已為君而疾病退罷者，當知古無此禮。

translations.literal: Annals record no reigning lord retiring for illness—antiquity knew no such ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Histories show no sick abdication precedent.

sentences.zh: 孟縶、穆子是方應為君，非陳留之比。」

translations.literal: Meng Zhi and Mu Zi were heirs presumptive—not comparable to Chenliu."
translations.idiomatic: Those Zuozhuan figures awaited succession unlike an enthroned charter king.

sentences.zh: 咸康四年，成帝臨軒，遣使拜太傅、太尉、司空。

translations.literal: Xiankang 4 Emperor Cheng faced south from the hall dispatching envoys to invest Grand Tutor, Grand Commandant, and Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Xiankang 4 Chengdi formally commissioned the three excellencies from the throne.

sentences.zh: 《儀注》，太樂宿懸於殿庭。

translations.literal: According to ceremony notes, the Directorate of Music lodged overnight instruments in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Liturgy manuals parked orchestral bells in the courtyard overnight.

sentences.zh: 門下奏，非祭祀宴饗，則無設樂之制。

translations.literal: The Chancellery reported that outside sacrifice and banquet no precedent sets music.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellery noted music belonged only to sacrifice or feast.

sentences.zh: 太常蔡謨議曰：「凡敬其事則備其禮，禮備則制有樂。

translations.literal: Chamberlain Cai Mo argued: 'Whenever reverence attaches, ritual follows complete; complete ritual implies regulated music.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo held solemn commissions deserve full ceremonial sound.

sentences.zh: 樂者，所以敬事而明義，非為耳目之娛，故冠亦用之，不惟宴饗。

translations.literal: Music exists to honor affairs and clarify duty—not for ear and eye pleasure—therefore even capping ceremonies use it, not only feasts.
translations.idiomatic: Music clarifies moral weight, not mere pleasure—hence cappings too employ it.

sentences.zh: 宴饗之有樂，亦所以敬賓也。

translations.literal: Feasts include music likewise to honor guests.
translations.idiomatic: Banquet music likewise honors guests.

sentences.zh: 故郤至使楚，楚子饗之，郤至辭曰：'不忘先君之好，貺之以大禮，重之以備樂。

translations.literal: Thus when Xi Zhi visited Chu, its lord feasted him; Xi declined saying: "Mindful of our former lords' friendship you granted grand ritual and doubled it with full orchestra.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zhi's Chu banquet refusal praised lavish music as intentional honor.

sentences.zh: '尋斯辭也，則宴樂之意可知矣。

translations.literal: From these words banquet music's intent is clear.
translations.idiomatic: His apology proves feast ensembles convey respect.

sentences.zh: 公侯大臣，人君所重，故御坐為起，在輿為下，言稱伯舅。

translations.literal: Dukes and chief ministers are what rulers esteem—therefore facing their seats he rises, meeting their carts he descends, speech calls them uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Sovereigns rise for great ministers and term them kin.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰'國卿，君之貳也'，是以命使之日，禦親臨軒，百僚陪列，此即敬事之意也。

translations.literal: The commentary says "state ministers are the ruler's deputies"; hence appointment day the imperial palanquin faces the hall while hundred officials flank—that shows reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Zuozhuan calls ministers the sovereign's second selves—investiture audiences mirror that awe.

sentences.zh: 古者，天王饗下國之使，及命將帥，遣使臣，皆有樂。

translations.literal: Antiquity's heavenly king feasted envoys from lesser states and commissioned generals or dispatched agents—always with music.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient kings used music for foreign envoys and outbound agents.

sentences.zh: 故《詩序》曰：'皇皇者華，君遣使臣也。

translations.literal: Therefore the Poetry preface says: "Splendid indeed those blossoms—the lord sends forth his envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Mao preface praises "Splendid blossoms" as king dispatching envoys.

sentences.zh: '又曰：'《采薇》以遣之，《出車》以勞還，《杕杜》以勤歸。

translations.literal: It also says: "Pick knotweed" sees him off, "Chariots roll out" welcomes return, "Pear-trunk" urges homeward toil.
translations.idiomatic: Prefaces tie "Caiwei," "Chuche," and "Ditu" to embarkation and homecoming songs.

sentences.zh: '皆作樂而歌之。

translations.literal: All were composed with music and sung.
translations.idiomatic: Each ode received musical setting.

sentences.zh: 今命大使，拜輔相，比于下國之臣，輕重殊矣。

translations.literal: Now commissioning great envoys to invest chief ministers compares to ministers of petty states—the weight differs vastly.
translations.idiomatic: Investing a chancellor outranks greeting a vassal envoy.

sentences.zh: 輕誠有之，重亦宜然。

translations.literal: Lightness indeed applies one way, heaviness should apply another.
translations.idiomatic: If petty missions deserve sound, weightier ones doubly so.

sentences.zh: 故謂臨軒遣使，宜有金石之樂。

translations.literal: Therefore we hold that facing the hall to dispatch agents ought to include bell-stone music."
translations.idiomatic: Thus palace-front commissions warrant bronze and stone.

sentences.zh: 」議奏從焉。

translations.literal: The memorial passed and was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Throne approved.

sentences.zh: 漢魏故事，王公群妾見於夫人，夫人不答拜。

translations.literal: Han–Wei precedent had royal dukes' concubine hosts presented to the principal wife without return bows.
translations.idiomatic: Old custom: chief consorts ignored concubines' bows.

sentences.zh: 新禮以為禮無不答，更制妃公侯夫人答妾拜。

translations.literal: New ritual held that ritual admits no unanswered courtesy—revising so consorts of princes and marquises return concubines' bows.
translations.idiomatic: New codes demanded reciprocation—noble wives bowed back.

sentences.zh: 摯虞以為：「禮，妾事女君如婦之事姑，妾服女君期，女君不報，則敬與婦同而又加賤也。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu argued: 'Ritual has concubines serving the mistress like daughters-in-law serving mothers-in-law; concubines mourn mistress one year without reciprocation—thus reverence matches daughters-in-law yet adds inferiority.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu noted concubines mourn principal wives without return—like daughters-in-law—emphasizing inferiority.

sentences.zh: 名位不同，本無酬報。

translations.literal: Names and stations differ—originally no answering courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Unequal rank never implied mutual bows.

sentences.zh: 禮無不答，義不謂此。

translations.literal: "Ritual admits no unanswered courtesy" does not mean this case.
translations.idiomatic: The general rule does not cover hierarchy.

sentences.zh: 先聖殊嫡庶之別，以絕陵替之漸。

translations.literal: Former sages emphasized distinction between legitimate and secondary to stop gradual encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: Sages separated primary from secondary to prevent usurpation.

sentences.zh: 峻明其防，猶有僭違。

translations.literal: They steeply fortified the barrier yet transgression still occurred.
translations.idiomatic: Even strict fences saw violations.

sentences.zh: 宜定新禮，自如其舊。

translations.literal: The new ritual ought to follow old practice."
translations.idiomatic: Retain silence toward concubine bows.

sentences.zh: 」詔可其議。

translations.literal: An edict approved his argument.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor endorsed Zhi Yu.

sentences.zh: 五禮之別，其四曰軍，所以和外寧內，保大定功者也。

translations.literal: Among divisions of the five rites the fourth is "military," whereby one harmonizes what lies beyond and pacifies what lies within, preserving greatness and fixing achievements.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth ritual category is "military": diplomacy abroad and stability at home, sustaining power and sealing victory.

sentences.zh: 但兵者凶事，故因搜狩而習之。

translations.literal: Yet arms are ill-omened affairs, hence through hunts and field exercises they drill them.
translations.idiomatic: Because warfare is inauspicious, drill came wrapped in seasonal hunts.

sentences.zh: 漢儀，立秋之日，自郊禮畢，始揚威武，斬牲於東門，以薦陵廟。

translations.literal: Han protocol: on Beginning of Autumn, once suburban sacrifice finished, they displayed martial majesty, slaughtered victims at the eastern gate, and offered them to mausoleum shrines.
translations.idiomatic: Han law tied autumn's start to suburban rites, then a martial parade, beast slaughter at the east gate, and offerings at imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 其儀，乘輿禦戎路，白馬硃鬣，躬執弩射牲，牲以鹿麛。

translations.literal: The ceremony: the imperial equipage took the war chariot, white horses with vermilion manes; personally he held crossbow and shot the victim—deer or fawn.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rode the martial carriage with white horses and red manes, shot the sacrificial deer himself.

sentences.zh: 太宰令謁者各一人載以獲車，馳送陵廟。

translations.literal: The senior butcher director and one usher each loaded it onto the hunt wagon and galloped it to the tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Butchery and usher officials carted the quarry to the ancestral park.

sentences.zh: 還宮，遣使者齎束帛以賜武官。

translations.literal: Returning to the palace, envoys bore bundled silk to reward military officers.
translations.idiomatic: Back at the palace couriers awarded silk to martial ranks.

sentences.zh: 武官肄兵，習戰陣之儀。

translations.literal: Military officials drilled troops and practiced battle formations.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers rehearsed arrays and maneuvers.

sentences.zh: 斬牲之禮，名曰<豸區>劉。

translations.literal: The beast-slaughter ceremony was named the chū-liù (貙劉) rite.
translations.idiomatic: This autumn killing drill bore the traditional name chū-liù.

sentences.zh: 兵官皆肄孫吳兵法六十四陣。

translations.literal: Commanders studied the sixty-four formations of Sunzi and Wuzi.
translations.idiomatic: Officers trained Sun and Wu's sixty-four tactical arrays.

sentences.zh: 既還，公卿已下陳<名隹>陽前街，乘輿到，公卿已下拜，天子下車，公卿親識顏色，然後還宮。

translations.literal: After returning, dukes downward lined the avenue before Zhuque Street in Luoyang; when the palanquin arrived they bowed; the Son of Heaven alighted so dukes could see his countenance—then he returned within.
translations.idiomatic: Nobles flanked Luoyang's south avenue; the emperor dismounted so ministers might glimpse him—the sole occasion for "alighting from the chariot."

sentences.zh: 古語曰在車下車，則惟此時施行。

translations.literal: An old saying says "dismount from the carriage"—only this moment implements it.
translations.idiomatic: The proverb about leaving the chariot applies uniquely here.

sentences.zh: 漢世率以為常。

translations.literal: The Han age routinely treated it as ordinary practice.
translations.idiomatic: Han made it an annual fixture.

sentences.zh: 至獻帝建安二十一年，魏國有司奏：「古四時講武，皆于農隙。

translations.literal: By Emperor Xian's twenty-first Jian'an year Wei authorities memorialized: 'Antiquity drilled arms four seasons, always in agricultural slack.
translations.idiomatic: Jian'an 21 Wei offices noted classical quarterly maneuvers during farm lulls.

sentences.zh: 漢西京承秦制，三時不講，惟十月都講。

translations.literal: Han Western Capital continued Qin practice—three seasons without drill; only the tenth month held capital-wide exercise.
translations.idiomatic: Western Han skipped three seasons like Qin, drilling only in the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 今金革未偃，士眾素習，可無四時講武。

translations.literal: Now metal and leather have not yet lain still yet troops are already practiced—we may omit four-season drilling.
translations.idiomatic: With war ongoing yet veterans seasoned, quarterly drill seemed redundant.

sentences.zh: 但以立秋擇吉日大朝車騎，號曰閱兵，上合禮名，下承漢制。

translations.literal: But on Beginning of Autumn choose an auspicious day for a great muster of chariots and horse—call it troop review—matching ritual nomenclature above and Han precedent below."
translations.idiomatic: Instead hold an autumn review named "inspecting troops," honoring both canon and Han usage.

sentences.zh: 」奏可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Throne assented.

sentences.zh: 是冬，閱兵，魏王親執金鼓以令進退。

translations.literal: That winter they reviewed troops; the Wei king personally beat gilded drums to signal advance and halt.
translations.idiomatic: Winter maneuvers saw Cao Cao beating golden drums for signals.

sentences.zh: 延康元年，魏文帝為魏王。

translations.literal: In first year of Yanxi Wei Emperor Wen was king of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxi 1 had Cao Pi as Wei king.

sentences.zh: 是年六月立秋，閱兵於東郊，公卿相儀，王禦華蓋，親令金鼓之節。

translations.literal: That year's sixth-month Beginning of Autumn they reviewed troops east of the capital; dukes directed ceremony; the king used a flowered canopy and personally set drum cadence.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth-month autumn review east of Ye featured royal canopy and Cao Pi's drum commands.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝太和元年十月，又閱兵。

translations.literal: Wei Emperor Ming, Tahe year one tenth month, again reviewed troops.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi repeated the review in Tahe 1/X.

sentences.zh: 漢魏故事，遣將出征，符節郎授節鉞於朝堂。

translations.literal: Han–Wei precedent: dispatching generals on campaign, the credential gentleman presented baton and axe in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: Old custom vested battle tokens in the hall via the insignia officer.

sentences.zh: 其後荀顗等所定新禮，遣將，禦臨軒，尚書受節鉞，依古兵書跪而推轂之義也。

translations.literal: Later Xun Yi and colleagues' new ritual had the sovereign face the hall while the secretariat received baton and axe—following ancient military texts' sense of kneeling to push the chariot axle.
translations.idiomatic: Revised code placed the emperor at the terrace while ministers handed tokens—echoing "pushing the axle" devotion.

sentences.zh: 五禮之別，其五曰嘉，宴饗冠婚之道於是乎備。

translations.literal: Among the five rites the fifth is "auspicious," whereby banquet, archery, capping, and wedding observances become complete.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth category is "celebratory": feasts, archery, capping, and weddings.

sentences.zh: 周末崩離，賓射宴饗之則罕復能行，冠婚飲食之法又多遷變。

translations.literal: When Zhou rule collapsed, guest archery and banquet rules rarely ran; capping, wedding, and food customs shifted repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's fall left archery feasts rare while crowning and marriage norms drifted.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》雖有服冕之數，而無天子冠文。

translations.literal: Though the Rites of Zhou counts crown-robes, it lacks text on the Son of Heaven's capping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhouli lists regalia but not imperial crowning.

sentences.zh: 又《儀禮》雲，公侯之有冠禮，夏之末造也。

translations.literal: The Book of Etiquette and Ceremonial states that marquises possessing capping rites were a late Xia invention.
translations.idiomatic: Yili notes aristocratic capping as a decadent Xia innovation.

sentences.zh: 王、鄭皆以為夏末上下相亂，篡弑由生，故作公侯冠禮，則明無天子冠禮之審也。

translations.literal: Wang Su and Zheng Xuan both hold that late Xia saw high and low in turmoil, usurpation and murder arising—therefore they fashioned marquis capping, proving definitively there was no Son of Heaven capping.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng and Wang read late Xia chaos producing lordly capping—proof no imperial ceremony existed.

sentences.zh: 大夫又無冠禮，古者五十而後爵，何大夫冠禮之有。

translations.literal: Great officers likewise lack capping rites—in antiquity one received noble rank only after fifty—why speak of officer capping?
translations.idiomatic: Ministers lack crowning because rank came after fifty.

sentences.zh: 周人年五十而有賢才，則試以大夫之事，猶行士禮也。

translations.literal: Zhou people at fifty with proven talent were tried on ministerial duties yet still observed knight ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou tested fifty-year prodigies as ministers while keeping lesser rites.

sentences.zh: 故筮日筮賓，冠於阼以著代，醮於客位，三加彌尊，皆士禮耳。

translations.literal: Hence divining day and guest, capping on the east stairs to show succession, toasting in guest position, three additions ever loftier—all knight ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Divination, eastern-step crowning, triple caps remain gentleman-grade liturgy.

sentences.zh: 然漢代以來，天子諸侯頗采其儀。

translations.literal: Yet since Han times Son of Heaven and feudatories largely borrowed its forms.
translations.idiomatic: Han onward emperors and princes adapted that framework.

sentences.zh: 正月甲子若丙子為吉日，可加元服，儀從冠禮是也。

translations.literal: An auspicious jiazi or bingzi day in first month could add the primary cap—protocol followed capping ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: First-month jiazi or bingzi suited the "first cap" per Yili.

sentences.zh: 漢順帝冠，又兼用曹褒新禮，乘輿初加緇布進賢，次爵弁、武弁，次通天，皆于高廟，以禮謁見世祖廟。

translations.literal: Emperor Shun's crowning also employed Cao Biao's new ritual: palanquin first added black cloth scholar cap, then noble cap and martial cap, finally tongtian—all in Gaozu shrine with ceremonial visit to Emperor Guangwu's temple.
translations.idiomatic: Shundi used Cao Biao's sequence—progressive caps ending at tongtian inside founder shrines.

sentences.zh: 王公已下，初加進賢而已。

translations.literal: Royal dukes downward began only with the advancing-scholar cap.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser nobles stopped at the first cap.

sentences.zh: 案此文，始冠緇布，從古制也，冠於宗廟是也。

translations.literal: Judging from this text the first cap's black cloth follows antiquity; crowning inside ancestral temple likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Black cloth first cap and shrine setting match classical intent.

sentences.zh: 魏天子冠一加。

translations.literal: Wei crowned Son of Heaven with a single addition.
translations.idiomatic: Wei emperors took one cap only.

sentences.zh: 其說曰：「士禮三加，加有成也。

translations.literal: The explanation runs: 'Knight ritual uses three additions because three marks completion.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: triple crowning completes a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 至於天子諸侯無加數之文者，將以踐阼臨下，尊極德備，豈得與士同也。

translations.literal: For Son of Heaven and feudatories texts lack addition counts because ascending the throne to face subjects means supremacy and virtue complete—how match common knights?
translations.idiomatic: Thrones need no triple repetition—sovereignty already "complete."

sentences.zh: 魏氏太子再加，皇子王公世子乃三加。

translations.literal: Wei crowned heir apparent twice, imperial sons and royal heirs thrice.
translations.idiomatic: Wei gave two stages to heirs, three to princes.

sentences.zh: 孫毓以為一加再加，皆非也。

translations.literal: Sun Yu held both single and double additions wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yu rejected Wei shortcuts.

sentences.zh: 《禮》醮辭曰：「令月吉曰，以歲之正，以月之令。

translations.literal: The Rites toasting prayer says: "On this auspicious day of this fine month—year's prime, month's command."
translations.idiomatic: Canon toast begins "propitious month and day."

sentences.zh: 」案魯襄公冠以冬，漢惠帝冠以三月，明無定月。

translations.literal: Judging therefrom, Duke Xiang of Lu received cap in winter while Emperor Hui of Han took his in the third month—showing no fixed month.
translations.idiomatic: Lu crowning in winter and Han in third month prove flexible timing.

sentences.zh: 而後漢以來，帝加元服咸以正月。

translations.literal: Yet Eastern Han onward every emperor's primary cap fell in first month.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han standardized New Year's month.

sentences.zh: 及咸寧二年秋閏九月，遣使冠汝南王柬，此則非必歲首。

translations.literal: In second Xianning year an intercalary ninth autumn month envoys crowned Prince Dong of Runan—proving not only year's beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Xianning 2's leap-month crowning broke the January rule.

sentences.zh: 禮冠於廟，然武、惠冠太子，太子皆即廟見，斯亦擬在廟之儀也。

translations.literal: Ritual crowns in temple; yet Emperors Wu and Hui crowned heirs who immediately visited shrine—imitating in-temple protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Though canon demands shrines, Jin heirs "visited" temples right after hall crowning.

sentences.zh: 穆帝、孝武將冠，皆先以幣告廟，訖又廟見也。

translations.literal: Emperors Mu and Xiaowu before crowning first announced with silk in temple, then again visited shrine afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Mu and Xiaowu offered silk notice before caps, then shrine audiences.

sentences.zh: 惠帝之為太子，將冠，武帝臨軒，使兼司徒高陽王珪加冠，兼光祿大夫屯騎校尉華暠贊冠。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui was heir awaiting crowning, Emperor Wu faced the hall, ordering concurrent Minister of Education Prince Gui of Gaoyang to place the cap and concurrent Minister of Works Hua Hao to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi presided as Prince Gui capped Hui with Hua Hao assisting.

sentences.zh: 江左諸帝將冠，金石宿設，百僚陪位。

translations.literal: South of the Yangzi, before each emperor's crowning, bronze and stone bands lodged overnight while hundred officials held stations.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Jin set orchestras overnight for imperial cappings.

sentences.zh: 又豫於殿上鋪大床，禦府令奉冕、幘、簪導、袞服以授侍中常侍，太尉加幘，太保加冕。

translations.literal: They spread a great couch in the hall beforehand; the imperial wardrobe director presented crown, turban, hairpin, guide, and robe to palace attendants; the grand mentor added turban, junior tutor added crown.
translations.idiomatic: Palace stewards laid out dais regalia; tutor and mentor staged turban then crown.

sentences.zh: 將加冕，太尉跪讀祝文曰：「令月吉日，始加元服。

translations.literal: About to add the crown the grand mentor knelt reading the prayer: "On this auspicious day we first add the cap.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Mentor knelt through the investiture prayer.

sentences.zh: 皇帝穆穆，思弘袞職。

translations.literal: August and reverend, the emperor ponders enlarging his robe's duties.
translations.idiomatic: Prayer praises solemn majesty embracing imperial burden.

sentences.zh: 欽若昊天，六合是式。

translations.literal: Revere so azure Heaven; the six directions take pattern from you.
translations.idiomatic: He models cosmos under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 率遵祖考，永永無極。

translations.literal: Following ancestors without end.
translations.idiomatic: He walks ancestral road endlessly.

sentences.zh: 眉壽惟祺，介茲景福。

translations.literal: May eyebrow-longevity bring blessing; great fortune attend."
translations.idiomatic: It prays for longevity and fortune.

sentences.zh: 」加冕訖，侍中系玄紞，侍中脫帝絳紗服，加袞服冕冠。

translations.literal: After crowning, attendants fastened black strings; attendants removed the emperor's crimson gauze robe and added robe and coronet.
translations.idiomatic: Then knots secured the crown and ritual robes replaced gauze.

sentences.zh: 事畢，太保率群臣奉觴上壽，王公以下三稱萬歲乃退。

translations.literal: When finished the junior tutor led ministers raising longevity cups; royal dukes downward thrice shouted "long life" before withdrawing.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Tutor toasted thrice-hailed longevity.

sentences.zh: 案《儀注》，一加幘冕而已。

translations.literal: According to ceremony notes only one turban-and-crown addition applied.
translations.idiomatic: Manuals record a single investiture layer.

sentences.zh: 泰始十年，南宮王承年十五，依舊應冠。

translations.literal: In tenth Taishi year Prince Cheng of Nangan turned fifteen and by precedent merited crowning.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi 10 Prince Cheng reached fifteen.

sentences.zh: 有司議奏：「禮，十五成童，國君十五而生子，以明可冠之宜。

translations.literal: Responsible offices memorialize: 'Ritual makes fifteen the finished boy; domain lords sire heirs at fifteen—showing crowning fitness.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars cited fifteen as canonical adult age.

sentences.zh: 又漢魏遣使冠諸王，非古典。

translations.literal: Moreover Han–Wei envoys crowning princes stray from classical antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: Dispatching envoys to cap kings broke old ritual.

sentences.zh: 」於是制諸王十五而冠，不復加使命。

translations.literal: Therefore regulation fixed princes crowning at fifteen without extra missions.
translations.idiomatic: Edict capped princes at fifteen without special envoys.

sentences.zh: 王彪之雲，《禮》、《傳》冠皆在廟。

translations.literal: Wang Biaozhi notes both Rites and commentary crown inside temple.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biaozhi recalled shrine crowning.

sentences.zh: 案成帝既加元服，車駕出拜於太廟，以告成也。

translations.literal: Judging from Emperor Cheng after adding cap his carriage exited to bow at Grand Temple—announcing completion.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdi visited Taizu shrine post-cap to "report completion."

sentences.zh: 蓋亦猶擬在廟之儀。

translations.literal: That likewise imitates being inside temple ritual.
translations.idiomatic: It mirrored shrine intent.

sentences.zh: 魏齊王正始四年，立皇后甄氏，其儀不存。

translations.literal: Wei King of Qi, fourth Zhengshi year, enthroned Empress Zhen—protocol does not survive.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Fang's Zhengshi 4 empress investiture is lost.

sentences.zh: 武帝咸寧二年，臨軒，遣太尉賈充策立皇后楊氏，納悼後也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu in second Xianning year faced the hall dispatching Grand Commandant Jia Chong with patent to establish Empress Yang—posthumous "mourning empress."
translations.idiomatic: Wudi used Jia Chong to enthrone Yang Yan, later canonized as dowager.

sentences.zh: 因大赦，賜王公以下各有差，百僚上禮。

translations.literal: Thereupon great amnesty; gifts scaled from royal dukes down; hundred officials presented congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Amnesty and ranked gifts followed.

sentences.zh: 太康八年，有司奏：「婚禮納徵，大婚用玄纁束帛，加珪，馬二駟。

translations.literal: In eighth Taikang year offices memorialized: 'Wedding protocol's bride-price: great weddings use black-and-red silk bundles plus jade tally and eight horses.
translations.idiomatic: Taikang 8 fixed imperial bride wealth: silk, jade, eight horses.

sentences.zh: 王侯玄纁束帛，加璧，乘馬。

translations.literal: Royal dukes use black-red bundles plus disk and yoked horses.
translations.idiomatic: Princes offered disks and teams.

sentences.zh: 大夫用玄纁束帛，加羊。

translations.literal: Great officers use black-red bundles plus sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers added sacrificial sheep.

sentences.zh: 古者以皮馬為庭實，天子加以谷珪，諸侯加大璋，可依周禮改璧用璋，其羊雁酒米玄纁如故。

translations.literal: Antiquity took hides and horses as courtyard gifts; Son of Heaven added grain-pattern jade, feudatories great half-disc—per Zhouli disks may become half-discs while sheep, goose, wine, rice, black-red silk remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: Classical court gifts paired pelts and horses with graded jade; Zhou swaps disk for half-disc.

sentences.zh: 諸侯婚禮，加納采、告期、親迎各帛五匹，及納徵馬四匹，皆令夫家自備。

translations.literal: Feudal wedding procedures add betrothal gifts, date announcement, and groom's escort—each five bolts silk—and bride-price four horses—all supplied by groom's house.
translations.idiomatic: Feudatories supplied silk stages and four horses themselves.

sentences.zh: 惟璋，官為具致之。

translations.literal: Only the half-disc the office provides.
translations.idiomatic: Officials furnished only the ceremonial jade.

sentences.zh: 」尚書硃整議：「案魏氏故事，王娶妃、公主嫁之禮，天子諸侯以皮馬為庭實，天子加以谷珪，諸侯加以大璋。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Zhu Zheng argued: 'Judging Wei precedent for princes taking consorts or princesses marrying, Son of Heaven and feudatories used hides and horses in courtyard; Son of Heaven added grain jade, feudatories great half-disc.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zheng cited Wei: royal weddings used pelts, horses, graded jade.

sentences.zh: 漢高後制聘，後黃金二百斤，馬十二匹。

translations.literal: Empress Lü's Han regulations for imperial engagement set two hundred catties gold and twelve horses.
translations.idiomatic: Han Empress Lü priced empress betrothal at two hundred jin gold.

sentences.zh: 夫人金五十斤，馬四匹。

translations.literal: Principal consorts fifty catties gold and four horses.
translations.idiomatic: Consorts fifty jin and four mounts.

sentences.zh: 魏氏王娶妃、公主嫁之禮，用絹百九十匹。

translations.literal: Wei royal weddings and princess dowries used one hundred ninety bolts silk.
translations.idiomatic: Wei used 190 bolts for princes and princesses.

sentences.zh: 晉興，故事用絹三百匹。

translations.literal: Since Jin arose precedent used three hundred bolts.
translations.idiomatic: Jin raised silk to three hundred.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「公主嫁由夫氏，不宜皆為備物，賜錢使足而已。

translations.literal: An edict replied: 'Princesses marry into husband houses—the court should not equip everything; grant cash sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Throne said princesses join husbands' households—cash stipends suffice.

sentences.zh: 惟給璋，餘如故事。」

translations.literal: Only supply the half-disc; other items follow old story."
translations.idiomatic: Provide ceremonial jade only; silk follows precedent.

sentences.zh: 成帝咸康二年，臨軒，遣使持節、兼太保、領軍將軍諸葛恢，兼太尉、護軍將軍孔愉，六禮備物，拜皇后杜氏。

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng second Xiankang year faced the hall dispatching commissioner concurrent Junior Tutor Guard-general Zhuge Hui and concurrent Grand Commandant Kong Yu with full six-rites gifts to invest Empress Du.
translations.idiomatic: Xiankang 2 Chengdi sent Zhuge Hui and Kong Yu with six ceremonies for Du Lingyang.

sentences.zh: 即日入宮，帝御太極殿，群臣畢賀。

translations.literal: Same day she entered palace; emperor sat Taiji Hall while assembled ministers congratulated.
translations.idiomatic: She entered Taiji that evening amid congratulations.

sentences.zh: 賀，非禮也。

translations.literal: Congratulations violate ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Such applause broke canon.

sentences.zh: 王者婚禮，禮無其制。

translations.literal: Royal wedding lacks prescribed ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: No classical chapter governs emperor's nuptials.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》「祭公逆王后于紀」，《谷梁》、《左氏傳》說與《公羊》又不同。

translations.literal: Spring and Autumn records Duke Ji fetching the queen from Ji—Guliang and Zuozhuan diverge from Gongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Annals lines on Duke Ji's queen-fetch spawn three commentary readings.

sentences.zh: 而自漢魏遺事，並皆闕略。

translations.literal: Since Han–Wei surviving affairs were largely omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Han–Wei archives barely documented them.

sentences.zh: 武、惠納後，江左又無復《儀注》。

translations.literal: After Wu and Hui empress investitures south of the Yangzi ceremony notes vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Post-Wu Eastern Jin lost manuals.

sentences.zh: 故成帝將納杜後，太常華恆始與博士參定其儀。

translations.literal: Therefore before Chengdi took Empress Du, Chamberlain Hua Heng first harmonized protocol with doctors.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Heng drafted rites for Du.

sentences.zh: 據杜預《左氏傳》說，主婚是供其婚禮之幣而已。

translations.literal: According to Du Yu's Zuozhuan gloss the ruler merely supplies wedding gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu said the throne only funded bride wealth.

sentences.zh: 又，周靈王求婚于齊，齊侯問于晏桓子，桓子對曰：「夫婦所生若如人，姑姊妹則稱先守某公之遺女若如人。

translations.literal: Moreover King Ling of Zhou sought marriage in Qi; Marquis of Qi asked Yan Huanzi who answered: "Children of husband and wife—if like others—or aunts and sisters call them "late lord So-and-so's surviving daughters like others."
translations.idiomatic: Zuozhuan frames Zhou–Qi matchmaking speeches.

sentences.zh: 」此則天子之命自得下達，臣下之答逕自上通。

translations.literal: Hence Son of Heaven's command reaches downward directly while ministers answer upward directly.
translations.idiomatic: Royal letters descend; replies ascend without middlemen.

sentences.zh: 先儒以為丘明詳錄其事，蓋為王者婚娶之禮也。

translations.literal: Earlier scholars thought Zuo detailed this because it records royal wedding etiquette.
translations.idiomatic: Exegetes treat the passage as imperial marriage template.

sentences.zh: 故成帝臨軒，遣使稱制拜後，然其《儀注》又不具存。

translations.literal: Therefore Chengdi faced the hall dispatching envoys with edict to invest the empress—yet surviving ceremony notes remain incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdi's hall commission survives but manuals stay fragmentary.

sentences.zh: 康帝建元元年，納皇后褚氏，而《儀注》陛者不設旄頭。

translations.literal: Emperor Kang first Jianyuan year took Empress Chu while ceremony notes omitted halberd-feather guards on the stairs.
translations.idiomatic: Kangdi's Chu wedding lacked maotou halberdiers per manual.

sentences.zh: 殿中御史奏：「今迎皇后，依成恭皇后入宮禦物，而《儀注》至尊袞冕升殿，旄頭不設，求量處。

translations.literal: Palace censors reported: 'Now welcoming the empress follows Honored Empress Cheng's palace inventory yet notes have the sovereign in coronation robe ascend without maotou—seek adjustment.
translations.idiomatic: Censors noted mismatch with Cheng Gong's precedent.

sentences.zh: 又案，昔迎恭皇后，惟作青龍旗，其餘皆即禦物。

translations.literal: Moreover formerly welcoming Honored Empress only raised azure-dragon banner—other items match ordinary imperial gear.
translations.idiomatic: Gong's entry used only azure-dragon flag.

sentences.zh: 今當臨軒遣使，而立五牛旗，旄頭罼{罒幹}並出即用，故致今闕。

translations.literal: Now facing the hall to dispatch envoys raises five-ox banner—maotou and feather screens deploy immediately—hence today's omission.
translations.idiomatic: New five-ox standards consumed escorts, explaining gaps.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「所以正法服、升太極者，以敬其始，故備其禮也。

translations.literal: The edict replied: 'We don full regalia and mount Taiji to honor the beginning—therefore ritual stands complete.
translations.idiomatic: Throne answered full dress honors inception.

sentences.zh: 今云何更闕所重而撤法物邪！

translations.literal: How now omit what matters and strip statutory gear!"
translations.idiomatic: Why strip regalia from what matters most!

sentences.zh: 又恭後神主入廟，先帝詔後禮宜降，不宜建五牛旗，而今猶復設之邪！

translations.literal: Moreover when Honored Empress Gong's spirit tablet entered the shrine the late emperor's edict lowered her observances—she ought not raise five-ox banners—yet now they persist!
translations.idiomatic: Gong's tablet entered under reduced honors forbidding five-ox standards—why revive them now?

sentences.zh: 既不設五牛旗，則旄頭罼{罒幹}之物易具也。

translations.literal: If five-ox banners are omitted, maotou plumes and feather screens become easy to supply.
translations.idiomatic: Dropping the five-ox pageant leaves halberd escorts and canopies easy to field.

sentences.zh: 」又詔曰：「舊制既難准，且於今而備，亦非宜。

translations.literal: A further edict said: 'Old regulations are hard to match; assembling everything today likewise misbehoves.
translations.idiomatic: Another decree conceded antiquity was elusive and full replication wasteful.

sentences.zh: 府庫之儲，惟當以供軍國之費耳。

translations.literal: Treasury stores ought only fund army and state expense.
translations.idiomatic: State coffers exist for war and administration.

sentences.zh: 法服儀飾粗令舉，其餘兼副雜器停之。」

translations.literal: Statutory robes and ritual ornaments should roughly suffice; other duplicated sundries cease."
translations.idiomatic: Issue minimal court dress; cancel redundant gear.

sentences.zh: 穆帝升平元年，將納皇后何氏。

translations.literal: In first Shenping year of Emperor Mu they were about to take Empress He.
translations.idiomatic: Mu's Shenping 1 planned Queen He's installation.

sentences.zh: 太常王彪之大引經傳及諸故事以定其禮，深非《公羊》婚禮不稱主人之義。

translations.literal: Chamberlain Wang Biaozhi cited canon, commentary, and precedents to settle ritual, deeply rejecting Gongyang's doctrine that weddings omit naming the host.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biaozhi blasted Gongyang's "no host" wedding theory.

sentences.zh: 又曰：'王者之于四海，無不臣妾，雖復父兄之親，師友之賢，皆純臣也。

translations.literal: He also said: 'The king toward the four seas lacks none who are subject concubines—even fathers, elder brothers, teachers, and wise friends count as pure ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Sovereigns own everyone as subjects—fathers and tutors included.

sentences.zh: 夫崇三綱之始，以定乾坤之儀，安有天父之尊，而稱臣下之命以納伉儷。

translations.literal: To elevate the three bonds' beginning and fix qian and kun's model—how can heaven-father's majesty use a subject's command to take a spouse?
translations.idiomatic: The cosmic order cannot have the father of heaven named by a minister's order to marry.

sentences.zh: 安有臣下之卑，而稱天父之名以行大禮。

translations.literal: How can a base subject invoke heaven-father's name to enact grand ritual?
translations.idiomatic: Nor may petty ministers invoke celestial father's style.

sentences.zh: 遠尋古禮，無王者此制；

translations.idiomatic: Inner palace requires eminent pedigree.

translations.idiomatic: Host reports pedigree request.

translations.idiomatic: Host trembles at lucky oracle.

translations.idiomatic: Wang Su's litany lists silk, paired skins, fowl, and sheep.

sentences.zh: 」前漢聘後，黃金二百斤，馬十二匹，亦無用羊之旨。

translations.literal: Former Han empress betrothal used two hundred catties gold and twelve horses—likewise no mandate for sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Western Han lacked ovine bride-price.

sentences.zh: 鄭氏《婚物贊》曰「羊者祥也」，然則婚之有羊，自漢末始也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan's Wedding Goods Praise says "sheep means auspice"—thus wedding sheep began only late Han.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's gloss ties sheep to felicity—a late Han innovation.

sentences.zh: 王者六禮，尚未用焉。

translations.literal: Royal six-rites had not yet employed them.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial weddings omitted sheep.

sentences.zh: 是故太康中有司奏：「太子婚，納徵用玄纁束帛，加羊馬二駟。」

translations.literal: Therefore Taikang offices memorialized: "Crown prince wedding bride-wealth uses black-red bundles plus sheep and eight horses."
translations.idiomatic: Taikang standardized heir weddings with sheep and eight mounts.

sentences.zh: 武帝泰始十年，將聘拜三夫人、九嬪。

translations.literal: In tenth Taishi year Emperor Wu was about to invest three ladies of senior rank and nine concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi 10 Wudi appointed three madames and nine imperial ladies.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「禮，皇后聘以谷珪，無妾媵禮贄之制。

translations.literal: Offices memorialized: 'Ritual invests empress with grain-pattern jade—no canonical tribute system exists for concubines.'
translations.idiomatic: Canon covers only empress dowry.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「拜授可依魏氏故事。

translations.literal: An edict replied: 'Investitures may follow Wei precedent.'
translations.idiomatic: Throne borrowed Wei forms.

sentences.zh: 」於是臨軒，使使持節兼太常拜三夫人，兼御史中丞拜九嬪。

translations.literal: Thereupon facing the hall they dispatched credential-bearing concurrent chamberlain to invest three madames and concurrent imperial censor-in-chief to invest nine ladies.
translations.idiomatic: Hall ceremony used chamberlain for madames, censor for nine ranks.

sentences.zh: 漢魏之禮雲，公主居第，尚公主者來第成婚。

translations.literal: Han–Wei ritual says princesses dwell in mansions—those marrying princesses conclude weddings at her estate.
translations.idiomatic: Han–Wei grooms visited princess residences.

sentences.zh: 司空王朗以為不可，其後乃革。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Wang Lang deemed it unacceptable—later they reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang protested until practice changed.

sentences.zh: 太元中，公主納徵以獸豹皮各一具禮，豈謂婚禮不辨王公之序，故取獸豹以尊崇其事乎！

translations.literal: During Taiyuan princess bride-wealth used leopard pelts—perhaps because wedding ritual blurred noble precedence and fierce pelts magnified the affair!
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan added leopard skins to stress royal dignity.

sentences.zh: 《禮》有三王養老膠庠之文，饗射飲酒之制，周末淪廢。

translations.literal: The Rites records three kings nurturing elders in schools with archery-feast drinking observances—late Zhou decayed them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou canon mandated elder care and village archery—lost in collapse.

sentences.zh: 漢明帝永平二年三月，帝始率群臣躬養三老五更於辟雍，行大射之禮。

translations.literal: In third month Yongping 2 of Han Mingdi the emperor first led ministers personally nurturing three elders and five seniors at Biyong, performing great archery.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi Yongping 2 opened classical elder ritual at the ring-shaped academy.

sentences.zh: 郡國縣道行鄉飲酒於學校，皆祠先聖先師周公孔子，牲乙太牢。

translations.literal: Commanderies, kingdoms, counties, and circuits held village drinking in schools, all sacrificing to former sages, former teachers, Duke of Zhou, and Confucius—using grand livestock offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Local schools offered tai-lao to Confucius and Zhou.

sentences.zh: 孟冬亦如之。

translations.literal: Midwinter likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Winter repeated the observance.

sentences.zh: 及魏高貴鄉公甘露二年，天子親帥群司行養老之禮。

translations.literal: By second Ganlu year of Wei Emperor Gaoguixiang the Son of Heaven personally led ministers performing elder-nurturing ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Caomao's Ganlu 2 revived imperial elder feast.

sentences.zh: 於是王祥為三老，鄭小同為五更。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wang Xiang served as chief elder and Zheng Xiaotong as associate elder.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiang and Zheng Xiaotong filled the elder seats.

sentences.zh: 其《儀注》不存，然漢禮猶在。

translations.literal: Though ceremony notes do not survive, Han ritual remains documented.
translations.idiomatic: Manuals vanished but Han precedent endures.

sentences.zh: 武帝泰始六年十二月，帝臨辟雍，行鄉飲酒之禮。

translations.literal: In twelfth month sixth Taishi year the emperor visited Biyong performing village drinking.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi Taishi 12/XII held village drinking at Biyong.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「禮儀之廢久矣，乃今復講肄舊典。

translations.literal: An edict said: 'Observances long lay ruined—now we again rehearse old canons.'
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed revival of forgotten rites.

sentences.zh: 」賜太常絹百匹，丞、博士及學生牛酒。

translations.literal: He gifted chamberlain one hundred bolts silk, assistants, doctors, and students oxen and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards went to ritual officers and students.

sentences.zh: 咸甯三年，惠帝元康九年，復行其禮。

translations.literal: Third Xianning year and ninth Yuankang year of Emperor Hui repeated the observance.
translations.idiomatic: Hui repeated it in Xianning 3 and Yuankang 9.

sentences.zh: 漢儀，季春上巳，官及百姓皆禊于東流水上，洗濯祓除去宿垢。

translations.literal: Han protocol: late spring shangsi day officials and commoners alike purified beside eastern flowing water, washing away accumulated grime.
translations.idiomatic: Han spring purification cleansed along eastward streams.

sentences.zh: 而自魏以後，但用三日，不以上巳也。

translations.literal: Yet since Wei they used only the third day—not tied to shangsi.
translations.idiomatic: Wei onward fixed the third lunar day.

sentences.zh: 晉中朝公卿以下至於庶人，皆禊洛水之側。

translations.literal: Under Jin's central court dukes downward to commoners purified along River Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang elites bathed at Luo.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫篡位，三日會天泉池，誅張林。

translations.literal: When Prince Zhao Lun usurped, on the third day they gathered at Tianquan Pool and executed Zhang Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lun's coup linked to Tianquan purification killing Zhang Lin.

sentences.zh: 懷帝亦會天泉池，賦詩。

translations.literal: Emperor Huai likewise convened at Tianquan Pool composing verse.
translations.idiomatic: Huaidi held poetry gatherings there.

sentences.zh: 陸機云：「天泉池南石溝引禦溝水，池西積石為禊堂。

translations.literal: Lu Ji notes: 'South of Tianquan Pool stone channels draw imperial ditch water; west of the pool piled stones form the purification hall.'
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji mapped Tianquan's hydraulic architecture.

sentences.zh: 」本水流杯飲酒，亦不言曲水。

translations.literal: Originally floating cups along running water served drinking games—it never mentions winding streams.
translations.idiomatic: Cup-float drinking predates "winding water" poetry.

sentences.zh: 元帝又詔罷三日弄具。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan further edicted abolishing third-day festival toys.
translations.idiomatic: Yuandi banned spring outing paraphernalia.

sentences.zh: 海西于鐘山立流杯曲水，延百僚，皆其事也。

translations.literal: Emperor Hai Xi established floating cups on winding water at Mount Zhong, extending invitations to hundred officials—same affair.
translations.idiomatic: Deposed emperor Haixi staged Zhongshan winding-stream banquet.

sentences.zh: 九月九日，馬射。

translations.literal: Ninth day ninth month—mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Double-ninth featured equestrian archery.

sentences.zh: 或說云「秋，金之節，講武習射，象立秋之禮也」。

translations.literal: Some explain: "Autumn belongs to metal's phase; drilling martial archery imitates Beginning-of-Autumn observances."
translations.idiomatic: Commentators tie autumn shooting to seasonal martial qi.
